Starting quarterback Jaxson Dart could be lost for the season due to a knee injury, so teams will likely gameplan to stop the run. That could mean tough sledding for the running game for the G-Men overall. However, in Week 3, the Giants will face a mediocre Titans run defense that has given up 120.5 rushing yards per tilt, which is 21st in the NFL. In addition, the Titans have already surrendered three rushing scores in the first two games of the season.

Darren Waller could remain a valuable part of the Panthers' offense in the Week 3 matchup against the Browns. Through two games, Waller appears to be the Panthers' top receiving option at tight end, leading the TE room in yards (66), receptions (five) and touchdowns (two). However, having only received five targets through two weeks, Waller is likely a touchdown-or-bust streaming option going forward. He's in for a tough Week 3 matchup against a Browns defense that's given up just 10.5 PPR fantasy points per game to the position this season.

outlooksByWeek.2: Kirk Cousins had a bumpy Raiders debut in a season-opening win over the Dolphins, completing 21 of 30 passes for 160 yards and three touchdowns with two interceptions. The veteran quarterback is just keeping the starting job warm for 2026 first overall pick Fernando Mendoza, but the team is in no hurry to get the rookie in the lineup before he's ready, and wins will only give Cousins more job security. His passing numbers could improve once star tight end Brock Bowers is cleared to play, as his most productive connection was running back Ashton Jeanty, who was on the other end of two of Cousins' TD passes. Cousins will face a Chargers defense in Week 2 that had trouble slowing down Jacoby Brissett in its opener but finished fourth in fantasy points per game allowed to QBs in 2025.
outlooksByWeek.3: Kirk Cousins has had an impressive start to the season, throwing three touchdowns in back-to-back games for a Raiders team that's a surprising 2-0. The veteran quarterback hasn't played completely mistake-free football under Klint Kubiak, throwing three interceptions, but he's only been sacked twice and has completed 67.8 percent of his passes. As long as Cousins remains productive and the team is winning, there will be little incentive for Las Vegas to hand the reins to rookie Fernando Mendoza, but that switch still figures to be coming at some point in 2026. Cousins will face a Saints defense in Week 3 that has done a good job holding Jared Goff and Lamar Jackson in check through its first two contests.

player.seasonOutlook: Cousins signed with the Raiders and will work as the team's starter to open the 2026 season ahead of No. 1 overall draft selection Fernando Mendoza. Cousins made eight starts for Atlanta last season and was not much of a fantasy option, averaging 12.5 fantasy points per game while reaching 18 points only once. The 38-year-old will be a bridge starter at best until Mendoza is ready and is no longer a threat with his legs (7 yards on 14 carries last season). He won't be a fantasy option, even when on the field. He should only be drafted late in superflex leagues.

outlooksByWeek.2: Antonio Williams led the Commanders in receiving in Week 1 despite playing just 26 offensive snaps. Williams ended up with four catches for 64 yards and a touchdown in his NFL premiere. He had as many targets as Terry McLaurin. Williams should see the field with increasing frequency if he continues to perform this well. He has a favorable matchup in Week 2 versus a Dallas defense that was the worst in the NFL last season, and surrendered three passing scores in the season-opening loss to the Giants.
outlooksByWeek.3: Antonio Williams snagged all three of his targets for 24 yards in the 37-20 loss to the Cowboys last game. Williams has seven catches for 98 yards and a touchdown through hsi first two NFL contests. Unfortunately, starting quarterback Jayden Daniels only played a half due to injury, so veteran backup Marcus Mariota will likely start in Week 3 versus a devastating Seattle defense. The Seahawks are allowing just 8.5 points per game thus far in 2026, which is second in the league. Seattle is also allowing the fewest passing yards per contest at 124.5 per tilt. None of this appears to be a recipe for success for Williams and the rest of the Washington offense.

player.seasonOutlook: Williams was selected by the Commanders in the third round of April's draft. He is an undersized slot receiver (75% slot in his collegiate career) who soaked up 208 catches (fourth most in this rookie class) during his four seasons (43 games) at Clemson. He was primarily a short-range option (8.0 aDOT), but he caught a healthy 75% of his targets and added value as a rusher (career 25-187-2 rushing), punt returner and even as a passer (143 yards and two TDs on four attempts). Williams is in an all-out battle with the likes of Dyami Brown, Luke McCaffrey, Jaylin Lane and Treylon Burks for the No. 3 WR gig behind Terry McLaurin and Stefon Diggs. He's worth no more than a late pick in deep leagues.

outlooksByWeek.2: Mike Gesicki and the Bengals are on the road in Week 2 to take on Houston. The Texans have the 27th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (19.7) to TEs, and they are last in receiving yards allowed to the position after Dalton Kincaid and Dawson Knox combined for 137 yards last week. Gesicki led the Bengals in catches (5), targets (7), and receiving yards (78) in Week 1, to go along with one TD. He could be primed for another big performance in what may very well be another high-scoring affair.
outlooksByWeek.3: Mike Gesicki and the Bengals are in Pittsburgh for an AFC North showdown in Week 3. After leading Cincinnati in receptions, yards, and targets in the season opener, Gesicki failed to record a single target versus the Texans in Week 2. Some of that could be chalked up to game flow with the Bengals ahead for most of the game, but it's nonetheless worrisome. The Steelers rank second in fantasy points allowed per game (5.5) and are first in receptions allowed to TEs through two weeks.

player.seasonOutlook: There was an era when Gesicki was a viable starting option in fantasy, but that time has come and gone. Since posting back-to-back top-eight fantasy campaigns in 2020 and 2021, Gesicki has finished 23rd, 37th, 13th and 41st the past four seasons. The latter came during a 2025 campaign in which he was limited to 41 targets in 13 games. Gesicki is no more than a situational seam stretcher and not much of an option near the goal line (he has exactly two TDs and five end zone targets each of the past three seasons). The 30-year-old will be a risky streaming option even if Ja'Marr Chase or Tee Higgins misses time.

outlooksByWeek.2: Samaje Perine and the Bengals travel to face the Texans for a Week 2 tilt. He was highly efficient with his touches in the season-opening win, tallying five carries for 20 yards while catching all three targets for 30 yards. Perine was the only other running back to record a carry, so his status as the No. 2 RB is not in question. Houston's defense is tied for third in fantasy points allowed per game (10.5) to RBs, but it surrendered 409 total yards of offense in their Week 1 loss to the Bills.
outlooksByWeek.3: Samaje Perine and the Bengals travel to take on the division-rival Steelers in Week 3. After dealing with an illness that forced him to miss two days of practice, he was active in Week 2 and recorded two carries for six yards and caught his lone target for 16 yards during Cincinnati's win over the Texans. With backfield mate Chase Brown handling 23 total touches, Perine's limited involvement on offense makes him a solid fantasy insurance policy, but nothing more. Pittsburgh's defense ranks 28th in rushing yards (233) and 29th in receiving yards allowed (97) to RBs.

player.seasonOutlook: Perine is expected to resume his role as Chase Brown's primary backup in Cincinnati. The veteran back played 31% of the Bengals' snaps last season, totaling 84 carries and 21 targets. He cleared 400 total yards for the fifth consecutive season, though he has yet to reach 200 touches in a single season in his career, nor has he produced a top-30 fantasy campaign. The 30-year-old has reached double-digit fantasy points three times over the last two seasons and would require a Brown injury in order to flirt with flex appeal. He can be left on waivers.

outlooksByWeek.3: Kaleb Johnson could continue to carve out a role as the Packers take on the Falcons in Week 3. Johnson saw a huge uptick in usage against the Jets in Week 2, logging eight carries for 32 yards. The second-year ball carrier was the most efficient of Green Bay's RBs, and he could continue to see an early-down role if MarShawn Lloyd remains inefficient. Still, Atlanta has allowed 127 rushing yards to running backs through two weeks, a top-10 mark, which could make Johnson's job tough even if he's the Packers' go-to on the ground.

player.seasonOutlook: Johnson was traded to Green Bay in August after his rookie season in Pittsburgh didn't go as planned. Drafted in the third round as a potential Najee Harris replacement, Johnson quickly found himself buried behind Jaylen Warren and Kenneth Gainwell and never recovered, even losing his kick returner role after a costly Week 2 blunder. He ended his first campaign with 78 yards on 29 touches. The 23-year-old will enter his second season with a fresh start and very well could get some early-season run with Josh Jacobs facing a suspension. Johnson will compete for reps with unproven Marshawn Lloyd and Chris Brooks. Keep him stashed in dynasty.

Despite leading the league in turnovers generated (33), the Bears' defense finished a middling 16th in fantasy points last season. The team subsequently replaced Jaquan Brisker, Kevin Byard and Tremaine Edmunds with Devin Bush, Coby Bryant and Dillon Thieneman during the offseason, meaning this will probably again be a matchups-oriented unit. Consider the Bears for favorable early matchups against the Panthers (Week 1) and Jets (4).

outlooksByWeek.2: Jalen Nailor didn't make much of a splash in his Raiders debut, catching three of five targets for 27 yards in a season-opening win over the Dolphins. All three of the team's top wideouts, including Tre Tucker and Jack Bech, produced very similar numbers, with Bech catching the trio's only TD. The group figures to remain secondary pieces in the passing game as RB Ashton Jeanty and TE Brock Bowers, when healthy, figure to be the top weapons for Kirk Cousins and, eventually, Fernando Mendoza. Nailor isn't likely to break out in Week 2 against a Chargers' secondary that finished last season tied for eighth in points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jalen Nailor has had a quiet start to his Raiders' tenure, catching four of eight targets for 36 yards through two games without a touchdown. He hasn't been able to get on the same page as quarterback Kirk Cousins, even though the two were together in Minnesota for the first two years of Nailor's career, and the impending return of Brock Bowers will bump everyone else down a rung in the pecking order for looks. Nailor seems unlikely to break out in Week 3 against a Saints secondary that ranks in the middle of the pack in terms of volume allowed to wide receivers so far, but which has given up three TDs to the position in two games.

player.seasonOutlook: Nailor signed with the Raiders and will battle the likes of Tre Tucker and second-year receivers Jack Bech and Dont'e Thornton Jr. for a starting gig in Las Vegas' new-look offense. Nailor was a rarely used commodity during his first four NFL seasons, all with the Vikings. The 2022 sixth-round pick totaled a 69-1,066-11 receiving line and never reached 30 catches or 450 yards in a single season. In fact, he's yet to clear six targets in a game. The 27-year-old very well could lock down a starting job in Las Vegas, but he's a long shot to make the big leap to consistent fantasy output in his fifth professional season. He's no more than a late-round wild card in deep leagues.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jake Elliott was perfect on all four of his kicks in Week 1 for the Eagles. Elliott connected on a 33-yard field goal as well as three extra points in the 24-22 win over the Commanders. In Week 2, Elliott will face a Titans squad that allowed a plethora of points last season. Tennessee gave up an average of 28.1 points per clash in 2025, which was 28th in the league.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jake Elliott nailed a 58-yard field goal in Philadelphia's last game. Elliott has not missed a kick through two games for the Eagles, connecting on two field goals and six PATs. In Week 3, the Eagles will face a Bears squad allowing 23 points per contest, which is in the middle of the pack thus far this NFL season.

outlooksByWeek.2: Cam Ward threw for just 140 yards in Tennessee's 23-10 Week 1 loss to the Jets, bringing the 2025 first-overall pick's career average down to 184 passing yards per game. He's best avoided for fantasy purposes, even in multi-QB formats, for the Titans' Week 2 home game against the Eagles. Philadelphia's stingy pass defense limited Jayden Daniels to 164 passing yards and 4.8 yards per pass attempt in the Eagles' season-opening win over Washington.
outlooksByWeek.3: Cam Ward will be tough to trust outside of deeper multi-QB formats in Week 3, when the Titans face the Giants on the road. The 2025 first overall pick scored two short rushing TDs in Tennessee's surprisingly competitive Week 2 loss to the Eagles, matching his career total in that category heading into that game. Ward has just one touchdown pass this season and 16 touchdown passes through 19 NFL starts, of which he has won three. The Giants allowed two touchdown passes to Dak Prescott and four to reigning MVP Matthew Stafford, but those two veteran QBs are far more effective passers than Ward at this stage in their respective careers.

player.seasonOutlook: Ward is eyeing a Year 2 leap following an underwhelming rookie campaign, albeit under tough circumstances. The 2025 No. 1 draft pick was plenty busy as a rookie (eighth in the league in dropbacks and pass attempts), but he struggled to 5.9 yards per attempt and took a league-high 55 sacks. Ward was rarely a factor with his legs (more than 12 yards three times) and produced one weekly fantasy finish better than 12th. The good news is that a tough rookie year isn't overly damning for a quarterback's career trajectory, and he'll be in a better spot in 2026 with new playcaller Brian Daboll and an improved supporting cast (Carnell Tate and Wan'Dale Robinson join a now-healthy Calvin Ridley). Ward will need to run more to become an elite fantasy option, but Year 2 is the breakout season for many quarterbacks, so he's well worth a late flier.

Run defense was the Bills' undoing last season, as they allowed a league-worst 24 rushing scores and snapped a seven-year streak of placing among the position's top 10 in fantasy points scored. Jim Leonhard was brought in as defensive coordinator, switching from a 4-3 to 3-4 scheme, though the team's personnel remains light up front. Regard the Bills a D/ST streaming candidate, and one better to leave undrafted due to their rough early schedule (@HOU, DET, LAC, NE, @LAR).

The Cowboys underwent a major roster overhaul and finished on a massive cold spell defensively late last season, making it difficult to get behind them as a fantasy option at the onset of 2026. Only the Jets scored fewer fantasy points for the year. The Cowboys did restock their roster during the offseason, adding Caleb Downs, Jalen Thompson and Rashan Gary (among others), and they do have a Giants matchup to open their schedule. It's still better to wait and see how this unit jells before diving in, however, even from a streaming standpoint.

outlooksByWeek.2: Deshaun Watson and the Browns visit the Buccaneers for an interconference clash in Week 2. In his first regular-season game since Oct. 20, 2024, Watson completed 16 of 22 pass attempts for 205 yards with one TD and one INT while rushing six times for 38 yards. Although his debut was uninspiring, head coach Todd Monken said he will stick with the 31-year-old as the starting quarterback after seeing enough positive glimpses on film. Watson will face another difficult matchup against Tampa Bay's 14th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (18.7) to QBs and therefore should remain on waiver wires.
outlooksByWeek.3: Deshaun Watson and the Browns host the Panthers for their home opener in Week 3. He completed 24 of 30 pass attempts for 238 yards with two TDs and no INTs, while rushing seven times for 22 yards during Cleveland's surprising Week 2 win over the Buccaneers. Watson led the comeback victory with scoring strikes of 55 and 17 yards, and chemistry appears to be brewing between him and the Browns' young playmakers. He'll face a Carolina defense that held the Falcons to 129 yards passing and forced three INTs and two fumbles in Week 2.

player.seasonOutlook: Watson will return to the field this season after a disastrous four years in Cleveland. A top-six fantasy QB (points per game) during each of his first four NFL seasons, Watson has appeared in a total of 19 games since joining the Browns, averaging a poor 13.1 fantasy points during the span. A torn Achilles suffered in Week 7 of 2024 (followed by tearing it again less than three months later) cost Watson all of 2025. Now 30 years old, with a young, unproven supporting cast and having not been a factor since 2020, Watson will open the season as Cleveland's starter, but he's a long shot to return to fantasy relevance. He should be considered only in superflex formats.

outlooksByWeek.2: Ray Davis remains largely uninvolved in the Bills' offense entering a Week 2 matchup with the Lions. He played more snaps on special teams (six) than on offense (five) in Week 1, and as long as James Cook remains healthy, Davis is an insurance policy more than a viable flex consideration. Davis' snaps would be further limited if RB Ty Johnson is able to suit up after missing Opening Week.
outlooksByWeek.3: Ray Davis has limited involvement in Buffalo's offense entering Week 3 against the Chargers. Through two weeks, Davis has logged one carry and no targets as James Cook's primary backup, making his only contribution on kick returns. Facing a defense that's allowing just 2.98 yards per carry and with no clear path to an uptick in opportunities, Davis is an insurance policy for Cook managers only.

player.seasonOutlook: Davis is back as the primary insurance option behind Bills' feature back James Cook III. The 2024 fourth-round pick is one of the most valuable backups in fantasy, but flies a bit under the radar due to a very small game-day role when Cook and passing-down specialist Ty Johnson are both healthy. That's been the scenario most of the last two seasons, but we've seen Davis play more than half of Buffalo's snaps in three games. During those outings, Davis averaged 21.0 touches, 130.3 yards and 19.4 fantasy points per game. The 26-year-old has no standalone value, but he'll leap into the RB2 mix should Cook miss time, which makes him worth stashing on the end of your bench.

outlooksByWeek.2: Geno Smith may be called upon more often in Week 2 when the Jets face the Packers. He wasn't asked to do much last week as the club played with a rare lead for the majority of the game, relying on the run-something unlikely to repeat in Week 2. Green Bay's secondary is vulnerable, allowing three touchdowns to Carson Wentz to start the year. With more volume, Smith can ascend to the second tier of quarterbacks in Week 2.
outlooksByWeek.3: Geno Smith will look to be the next quarterback to take advantage of the Lions' secondary when the Jets head to Detroit in Week 3. Smith hasn't topped 250 yards through two games and has just one touchdown pass, but he is in a very favorable spot in Week 3, with Detroit having allowed three touchdown passes in each outing thus far. Smith threw 41 times in Week 2, and so long as the Lions are scoring, Smith will likely have high volume again, putting him in a position to have his best showing of the year.

player.seasonOutlook: Smith was traded to the Jets following an unsuccessful one-year stint in Las Vegas. Smith, who began his career as a second-round pick with the Jets in 2013, is in line to start, though he's a long shot for consistent fantasy production. Smith peaked with a ninth-place finish in fantasy points per game with Seattle in 2022, but he has finished no better than 16th over the past three seasons. He paced the NFL in both interceptions and sacks in 2025 after finishing third in both categories in 2024 and is no longer much of a factor with his legs. The 35-year-old might bring some stability to the fantasy outlook of the team's pass catchers, but we shouldn't expect much more than that. Consider Smith only in superflex formats.

outlooksByWeek.2: Najee Harris was a healthy scratch in Week 1 for the Giants, but that could change quickly. While Cam Skattebo and Devin Singletary look like the 1-2 duo out front, third-string running back Tyrone Tracy lost a fumble in the red zone that could have proven costly.  Tracy had a rough camp even before the gaffe, so his time on the Giants could be coming to an end. If Harris does suit up in Week 2, he will be facing a Rams defense that was surprisingly suspect against the run in their first game of the season.  The Rams allowed 174 yards on the ground, which currently ranks them 30th in the league. However, Aaron Donald will return to the fold out of retirement versus the G-Men.

Keon Coleman doesn't appear to have a meaningful role in the Bills' offense entering Week 2 against the Lions. Despite playing 52% of the team's offensive snaps, Coleman drew only one target, which resulted in a one-yard catch. Always a candidate for an end-zone jump ball, Coleman is no better than fourth in the target pecking order, suggesting he's unlikely to contribute despite an inviting matchup against a secondary that allowed 410 passing yards in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Keon Coleman will look to build on a mild breakout when the Bills face the Chargers in Week 3. He hauled in six passes last week, his highest total since Week 1 of 2025, as the Bills lost DJ Moore (shoulder) early in Week 2. The Chargers have been more vulnerable to slot options than bigger outside receivers, and Moore's availability remains in flux. With the Bills offense clicking at all levels, Coleman can still garner enough volume to be a deep-league flex consideration.

player.seasonOutlook: So far, so bust for Coleman, who has struggled to make an impact after being selected 33rd overall in the 2024 draft. After flashing in a situational deep-threat role as a rookie (15.0 aDOT), Coleman saw more high percentage looks in 2025 (11.2 aDOT). That led to a much better catch rate (from 51% to 66%), but a big dip in yardage (19.2 YPR to 10.9). Coleman has yet to emerge as a reliable, full-time starter and was even a healthy scratch at times last season. Perhaps the 23-year-old will make a Year 3 leap with Joe Brady now running the show, but he'll have his hands full overtaking DJ Moore and Khalil Shakir atop the depth chart. Coleman is only worth a late flier in deeper leagues.

outlooksByWeek.2: Aaron Rodgers and the Steelers visit the Patriots for a Week 2 road clash. He completed 24 of 40 pass attempts for 221 yards with one TD and no INTs while rushing three times for minus-3 yards during Pittsburgh's 20-13 Week 1 victory over the Falcons. The Steelers attempted 41 passes compared to just 21 rushing attempts, as Rodgers connected with seven different receivers on the day. They'll face a tougher test on the road against New England's eighth-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (15.3) to QBs.
outlooksByWeek.3: Aaron Rodgers and the Steelers host the division-rival Bengals in Week 3. He threw for 187 yards (23-for-39) with no touchdowns and one INT and lost one of his two fumbles during Pittsburgh's Week 2 loss to the Patriots. Cincinnati has been somewhat stingy against opposing QBs, allowing 20.2 fantasy points through two outings (15th) despite giving up 353 passing yards versus Houston in Week 2. The Bengals are the only defense without an interception to this point, but they're also the only team that has yet to surrender a passing TD.

player.seasonOutlook: Rodgers re-signed with the Steelers and will return for his second season with the team. The 42-year-old is reuniting with his longtime head coach from Green Bay, Mike McCarthy. The duo will look to improve on a 2025 campaign in which Rodgers finished just outside the top 12 in passing yards and touchdowns while ranking 23rd among 28 qualified QBs in QBR. Even if Rodgers' efficiency improves, he remains a nonfactor as a rusher (he last cleared 107 yards in 2020) and hasn't been fantasy relevant since 2021 (25th, 18th and 25th in points per game in his past three full seasons). Even with a more pass-friendly playcaller and with Michael Pittman Jr. and Germie Bernard added to the wide receiver room, Rodgers is no more than a low-ceiling QB2.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jaylin Noel finished second on the Texans with 53 receiving yards in the season opener despite being targeted just twice. Noel will need to earn a larger role to gain fantasy relevance, but he has a chance to do so given Houston's lack of a clear No. 2 WR behind Nico Collins. Xavier Hutchinson and Kayshon Boutte combined for eight targets in Week 1 but recorded only 53 receiving yards between the two of them, matching Noel's yardage total. Noel can't be trusted as a starter heading into a Week 2 home game against the Bengals, but the 2025 third-round draft pick could be worth stashing, especially in deeper formats.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jaylin Noel could see extra opportunities in Week 3 if Texans WR Nico Collins (hamstring) misses a second consecutive game against the Colts. Noel has just three catches this season, but two of them have exceeded 30 yards. The 2025 third-round pick's big-play ability makes him a viable deep-league option in Week 3 against a Colts defense that has allowed the most points and yards in the NFL through two games. Xavier Hutchinson, Kayshon Boutte, and Jared Wayne are the other healthy options in Houston's WR room.

outlooksByWeek.2: Spencer Shrader made a 58-yard field goal but also missed an extra point in a confounding performance during the Colts' season-opening loss. The big-legged kicker may not get many opportunities in Week 2 against the Chiefs, especially since the Colts are one of the league's most efficient red-zone teams thanks to the presence of star RB Jonathan Taylor. Shrader is a middling fantasy option, and you can likely find a kicker in a more appealing situation on your league's waiver wire.
outlooksByWeek.3: Spencer Shrader has made all four of his field-goal attempts and five of six extra point tries through two games this season. The Colts are averaging a robust 26.5 points per game, but their success on offense has been overshadowed by a league-worst defensive performance en route to a 0-2 start. Shrader is gaining some streaming appeal heading into a Week 3 home game against the Texans, who are allowing 28.0 points per game in the early going after giving up just 17.4 points per game last season. He's a borderline fantasy starter at this point.

outlooksByWeek.2: Mack Hollins will look to capitalize on an elevated role in Week 2 when the Patriots face the Steelers. Hollins caught four of his five targets to open the year, finishing with 51 yards, and could slide into A.J. Brown's (ankle) vacated outside role. Hollins and DeMario Douglas have the trust of Drake Maye, something that can't currently be said for Romeo Doubs, suggesting Hollins will play against a secondary that's without top corner Joey Porter Jr. Hollins' size makes him a capable red zone target, which generates upside.
outlooksByWeek.3: Mack Hollins will seek a bounce back performance in Week 3 when the Patriots face the Jaguars. After a solid four catch, 51-yard opener with A.J. Brown leaving early, Hollins notched only two targets in Week 2. New England's passing game is struggling with Drake Maye completing just 14 passes in Week 2. Until he begins to bounce back, trusting any of his pass catchers appears a risky proposition even against a defense that is allowing a generous 10.3 yards per target.

outlooksByWeek.2: Wil Lutz's opportunities were minimal in the Broncos' season-opening loss to Kansas City, converting his only extra point and his sole field-goal attempt from 31 yards. The veteran kicker had been productive in his first three years with Denver, averaging just under 30 FGs and 38 extra points per season while going 12-for-18 on field-goal attempts of 50-plus yards. In Week 2, Lutz will take on a Jaguars team that ranked eighth in points per game allowed in 2025.
outlooksByWeek.3: Wil Lutz has been perfect to begin the season for the Broncos, and in a Week 2 win over the Jaguars, he converted both his field-goal attempts and both his PATs. The veteran kicker has been consistent since following Sean Payton northwest from New Orleans, and kicking at altitude has allowed him to be reliable from long range, but the Denver offense doesn't provide him with enough opportunities to be among the elite at his position. Lutz will face a Rams team in Week 3 that just kept the Giants out of the end zone but which has allowed five FG attempts through two games.

player.seasonOutlook: Mendoza was selected by the Raiders with the No. 1 overall pick in April's draft. The reigning Heisman Trophy winner and national champion, Mendoza is a big, pocket quarterback with elite accuracy (his career 7.1% off-target rate is easily the best in this rookie class) and a solid arm. Mendoza's 2025 campaign at Indiana included class-best marks in passing TDs (41) and QBR (90.3). He posted a 65-440-7 rushing line in 16 games last season and figures to add some value with his legs in the pros. Mendoza will get some run as a rookie, but his supporting cast isn't overly impressive and he will not start in Week 1 (Kirk Cousins will get the call), so there's not much sense in drafting him in most formats. He'll be worth a speculative add only when he's named Las Vegas' starter.

While the Saints showed improvement under first-year defensive coordinator Brandon Staley over the course of 2025 -- their 66 fantasy points following their Week 11 bye was fifth-best in the league -- the team has a rough go of it at the onset of 2026. Road matchups with the Lions (Week 1) and Ravens (2) are tough as nails, and even the addition of LB Kaden Ellis isn't going to ease those matchup worries. Consider this a streaming defense at best.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jauan Jennings will aim to make more of his opportunities as the Vikings take on the Bears in Week 2. Jennings garnered just one target against the Packers in Week 1, and he was unable to convert it into a reception. The veteran was still on the field for almost half of the offensive plays, which keeps him as the WR3 moving forward. He'll look to get his first catch of the season against a Chicago defense that allowed the fourth-most PPR points to Panthers wide receivers (46.3) in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jauan Jennings will hopefully return to action as the Vikings travel to Tampa Bay in Week 3. Jennings sat out in Week 2 due to personal reasons, so his practice availability this upcoming week should dictate whether he plays at the Bucs. The former 49ers wideout has yet to record a catch this season, but he played almost 50 percent of the offensive snaps in Week 1. He'll face a Bucs defense that's allowed 24.9 PPR points per game against wide receivers so far this season, a top-10 mark.

player.seasonOutlook: Jennings signed with the Vikings in May. The 2020 seventh-round pick was a situational player during his first three pro campaigns in San Francisco prior to breaking out with a 77-975-6 receiving line and 27th-place finish in fantasy PPG in 2024. He dipped quite a bit statistically in 2025 and failed to produce a single top-10 fantasy week, but did score nine touchdowns (sixth among WRs) in a good Niners offense. The 29-year-old will now file in third on the Minnesota depth chart behind Justin Jefferson and Jordan Addison. He's headed for a big dip in targets and, especially with Kyler Murray under center, won't be a consistent fantasy option. He's barely worth late-round consideration.

outlooksByWeek.2: Evan Engram was on the receiving end of Bo Nix's only touchdown pass in the Broncos' season-opening loss to Kansas City. The veteran tight end also led the team in receiving yards with a 4-43-1 line on five targets, as top wideouts Jaylen Waddle and Courtland Sutton were neutralized. Engram's first season in Denver was a disappointment, as his 461 receiving yards last year were his lowest total for a full season since 2021, but more experience in Sean Payton's scheme and a new play-caller in Davis Webb could lead to better numbers. Engram is set for a potential revenge game in Week 2 against a Jaguars defense that ranked 23rd in points per game allowed to TEs last season.
outlooksByWeek.3: Evan Engram had a minimal role in the Broncos' Week 2 win over the Jaguars, catching his only target for 17 yards. The veteran tight end has notched just six targets through two games, and while he did get into the end zone in the season opener, the reduced volume he saw in 2025, his first year in Denver, doesn't look like it will improve in 2026. Engram will take on a Rams defense in Week 3 that's allowed just 64 receiving yards to TEs so far, sixth in the league, and has yet to allow one to score a touchdown.

player.seasonOutlook: Engram returns for his second season in Denver after an underwhelming debut campaign with the team. The veteran tight end was limited to a career-low 13% target share and finished 15th or lower among tight ends in routes, targets, catches and yardage, despite appearing in 16 games. Engram worked as a short-area target but still struggled to a poor 68% catch rate and was, as usual, a nonfactor near the goal line (one TD, two end zone targets). Engram hasn't cleared four touchdowns in a season since he scored six as a rookie in 2017. He finished 32nd among tight ends in fantasy PPG and isn't a good bet for a larger role this season, especially with Jaylen Waddle added to the offense. The 32-year-old Engram is a fantasy TE3, at best.

outlooksByWeek.2: AJ Barner is coming off a quiet season opener as Seattle heads to Arizona in Week 2. Barner logged just two catches on two targets for 13 yards against the Patriots last Wednesday, though those two receptions were tied for second-most on the squad. Drew Lock played most of that game at QB for Seattle, and he's expected to start in Week 2 with Sam Darnold dealing with a glute injury. The Cardinals gave up seven catches for 90  yards to Chargers tight ends in a win Sunday, so Barner could be a key target for Lock.
outlooksByWeek.3: AJ Barner should again lead Seattle's TE corps in a Week 3 tilt versus Washington. Barner logged a healthy 56 of the Seahawks' 70 offensive snaps Sunday versus the Cardinals, but he finished with just one catch (on one target) for eight yards. Barner did boost his fantasy line considerably with a rushing touchdown, though his three catches for 21 yards through two weeks isn't going to turn many heads. Nonetheless, he could be a sneaky option for Week 3 against a Commanders defense that has already given up four receiving TDs to tight ends, tied for most in the NFL.

player.seasonOutlook: Barner was a solid contributor for the Seattle offense last season. The 2024 fourth-round pick worked his way to the top of the depth chart, and although his overall volume was limited (20th among TEs in targets and yards), he found the end zone seven times and finished 14th in fantasy points (21st in PPG). The 24-year-old is a serviceable, short-range target for Sam Darnold, but even with some rushing worked in, his role in Seattle's low-volume passing offense won't allow much upside. In fact, it's possible he loses some targets to second-year TE Elijah Arroyo this season. Barner is a fringe TE2, at best.

Hill is currently a free agent after being released by Miami. One of the top fantasy players of the past decade, Hill's best days may be behind him as he enters his age-32 campaign. The former fifth-round pick was fantasy's top-scoring receiver from 2017-23, but struggled to an 18th-place finish in 2024 (31st PPG) and then suffered a season-ending knee injury in Week 4 of last season. If he's able to play in 2026, Hill may still be able to hit for the occasional explosive play, but considering his age and the major injury, his ceiling is likely that of a boom/bust flex.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jacoby Brissett will look to help Arizona pull off another upset against Seattle in Week 2. Brissett was great in a season-opening win over the Chargers, throwing for 277 yards with a touchdown and no interceptions. His passing score went to tight end Trey McBride, who should continue to be his top weapon as one of the league's top players at the position. The Seahawks present a tough challenge, however, as they are expected to have one of the league's top defenses and picked Drake Maye off three times in a Week 1 win.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jacoby Brissett will look to bounce back from a poor performance when Arizona faces the 49ers in Week 3. Brissett recorded just 95 passing yards with one touchdown and one interception Sunday in a loss to Seattle, with that yardage being less than half of his previous low mark across any of his 16 starts for the Cardinals. Still, McBride was able to maintain his rapport with star tight end Trey McBride, as the pair connected for 41 yards and a touchdown through the air. Brissett's path to a rebound isn't an easy one, as San Francisco has given up just 11.8 fantasy points per game to QBs -- the second-fewest in the league -- through two weeks.

player.seasonOutlook: Brissett is back for his second season in Arizona and is currently positioned as the team's probable Week 1 starter. One of the biggest fantasy surprises of 2025, Brissett reeled off nine consecutive top-12 fantasy outings spanning Weeks 6 to 15. He averaged 18.9 fantasy points across 12 starts, which was a big surprise considering his prior career high was 12.9, and that was way back in 2017. Brissett played solid ball, but he's not a major contributor with his legs (260 yards is his career high for a season). He certainly benefited from the league's pass-heaviest offense, a luxury he's unlikely to have with Mike LaFleur now calling plays. Expect the 33-year-old to regress to fringe QB2 production, and keep in mind that it's possible Arizona will turn to rookie Carson Beck at some point this season.

outlooksByWeek.2: Xavier Hutchinson remains off the fantasy radar in most formats heading into Houston's Week 2 home game against the Bengals. He was third on the Texans with six targets in the season opener but finished with just three catches for 32 receiving yards. Hutchinson has topped 42 yards just twice through 50 career regular-season appearances.
outlooksByWeek.3: Xavier Hutchinson drew nine targets in Nico Collins' (hamstring) absence in Week 2 but turned that into just three catches for 37 yards. Hutchinson figures to maintain a prominent role in Houston's passing game against the league-worst Colts defense in Week 3, especially if Collins remains sidelined. Whether Hutchinson can turn that significant usage into production is another matter, as he has usually failed to capitalize on such opportunities in the past, with only two career regular-season games of 42 or more receiving yards. Hutchinson is in the Week 3 deep-league flex conversation, but his lack of prior production is concerning.

outlooksByWeek.2: Chig Okonkwo had a rough debut Week 1 for the Commanders. On only three targets, the former Titan caught a mere two passes for 16 yards in the 24-22 loss to the Eagles. He subsequently injured his hamstring and did not return. Meanwhile, both Stefon Diggs and rookie Antonio Williams found the end zone in their respective debuts for Washington. John Bates and Ben Sinnott would step in at tight end if Chig misses Week 2 versus Dallas. If he suits up, Okonkwo would have a favorable matchup against a Cowboys defense that allowed two touchdowns to Giants tight end Isaiah Likely in the season opener.
outlooksByWeek.3: Chig Okonkwo did not play in Week 2 for the Commanders. Washington's active tight ends did not fare well, catching a combined two passes for 20 yards in the 37-20 loss to Dallas. Starting quarterback Jayden Daniels only played a half due to injury, and veteran backup Marcus Mariota will likely start in Week 3 versus a devastating Seattle defense. The Seahawks are allowing just 8.5 points per game thus far in 2026, which is second in the league. Seattle is also allowing the fewest passing yards per contest at 124.5 per tilt. None of this appears to be a recipe for success for Okonkwo, even if he is able to suit up.

player.seasonOutlook: Okonkwo signed with the Commanders after spending his first four seasons in Tennessee. The 2022 fourth-round pick is one of only four tight ends who have appeared in all 68 games since he entered the league, and he's also one of only six tight ends who have registered 50-plus receptions each of the past three seasons. On the other hand, Okonkwo has yet to clear a 16% target share in a single season, and he has been a nonfactor near the goal line (eight TDs and 11 end zone targets in his career). As a result, he has finished exactly 21st in fantasy points each of the past three seasons. Perhaps he'll make a leap as one of Jayden Daniels' top targets, but the 27-year-old is no more than a back-end TE2 lottery ticket.

outlooksByWeek.2: Daniel Carlson will look to remain productive in the Saints' Week 2 matchup against the Ravens. Carlson converted his first four kicks (two field goals and two extra points) before missing a 62-yard field-goal attempt on the last play of regulation. He's expected to have plenty of scoring opportunities moving forward but may struggle against the Ravens in Week 2, as they allowed just 5.0 kicking points in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Daniel Carlson is expected to have few scoring opportunities in the Saints' Week 3 matchup against the Raiders. Carlson, who spent the previous eight seasons with the Raiders, converted on all three of his field-goal tries during the Week 2 win over the Ravens. He could continue to receive scoring opportunities due to New Orleans' offensive success. However, Carlson is likely in for a difficult Week 3 matchup, as Las Vegas has allowed just 4.5 kicking points per game this season.

outlooksByWeek.2: Michael Penix (knee) is expected to operate as Atlanta's starting quarterback if available for the Week 2 matchup against the Panthers, whose defense allowed 59 points to the Bears in Week 1. Penix has appeared in just 14 games during his two NFL seasons, throwing for 2,757 yards, 12 touchdowns and six interceptions. While healthy last season, Penix lead the Falcons to a 3-6 record while the offense averaged 20.6 points per game. He should be in for a very favorable matchup, with Carolina's defense giving up 40 fantasy points to Caleb Williams last week.
outlooksByWeek.3: Michael Penix is slated to make his 2026 debut during the Falcons' Week 3 matchup against the Packers. Atlanta has struggled offensively with Cooper Rush and Jack Strand as the team's quarterbacks over the last two weeks, scoring just 16 total points while Rush and Strand accounted for seven turnovers. However, Penix led the Falcons' offense to 20.6 points per game while throwing for 220.2 yards per game when healthy in 2025, suggesting improvement could be coming. Penix will be in for a tough matchup though, as Green Bay's defense has given up just 19.2 fantasy points per game to opposing QBs this season.

player.seasonOutlook: Penix is no longer guaranteed a starting job entering his third season. The 2024 first-round pick has appeared in 14 games and has 14 total touchdowns, a 21% off-target rate and a 60% completion percentage to show for it. Penix has done well to avoid turnovers (six career INTs), but he's a nonfactor with his legs (career 28-81-2 rushing) and failed to post a single fantasy outing better than 10th last season. Penix tore an ACL in Week 11, which further complicates his path to beating out newcomer Tua Tagovailoa for the team's Week 1 starting gig. The 26-year-old might eventually emerge into a fine NFL starter, but even if he does, his lack of rushing will limit his fantasy output. He's well off the fantasy radar.

The Raiders have a lengthy track record of defensive struggles, finishing in the upper half of the league in fantasy points from the D/ST in only one of the past 15 seasons. Still, the team added LBs Nakobe Dean and Quay Walker and CB Taron Johnson during the offseason, and it does still have DE Maxx Crosby on board. There could be some streaming potential here in favorable Weeks 1 (MIA) and 3 (@NO) matchups.

outlooksByWeek.2: Germie Bernard and the Steelers are on the road for a Week 2 battle with the Patriots. The rookie should remain on waiver wires after playing just three of Pittsburgh's 67 offensive snaps in their season-opening win. Bernard is below DK Metcalf, Michael Pittman, Jaylen Warren, Rico Dowdle, and Pat Freiermuth on the food chain, and it would take an absence or two from his teammates for him to see an uptick in playing time.
outlooksByWeek.3: Germie Bernard and the Steelers host the Bengals for a Week 3 divisional showdown. With Michael Pittman (foot) on the sidelines last Sunday, the rookie stepped into the No. 3 receiver role behind DK Metcalf and Roman Wilson. Bernard caught four of eight targets for 35 yards in the 20-3 loss, seemingly earning the trust of Aaron Rodgers rather quickly. He led the team in yardage, was second in targets, and tied for second in receptions. Bernard faces Cincinnati's 9th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed (25.0) to WRs and should be considered a roster stash until we see this type of performance consistently.

player.seasonOutlook: Bernard was selected by the Steelers in the second round of April's draft. Bernard is a solid, reliable receiver with good size who can align all over the formation (55% slot in 53 collegiate games). Despite playing at three schools in four years, Bernard's production increased each season, including a strong 64-862-7 receiving line (plus 18-101-2 rushing) in 2025. He dropped only four of 240 career targets. Bernard is likely to open his career third or fourth in line at receiver behind Michael Pittman Jr., DK Metcalf and perhaps Roman Wilson. That will create a tough path to consistent rookie-season usage and production, so he's only worth draft consideration in the later rounds.

outlooksByWeek.2: Nick Folk will look to bounce back from a tough performance in the Falcons' Week 2 matchup against the Panthers. The 41-year-old went made just three of the five kicks he attempted in the Week 1 loss, missing field-goals from 54 and 45 yards. He could be in line to continue receiving scoring opportunities, with Atlanta's offense struggling to find the end zone last week. Additionally, Folk is in for a great matchup, with Carolina allowing 11 kicking points in a Week 1 loss to the Bears.
outlooksByWeek.3: Nick Folk's early-season struggled could continue in the Falcons' Week 3 matchup against the Packers, who have allowed just 6.0 kicking points per game this season. Through two games in 2026, Folk has made just three of six field-goal tries, which is the worst mark in the NFL. He could benefit from the return of quarterback Michael Penix, however, who is expected to drive improvement after Atlanta's offense averaged just 8.0 points per game prior to his return.

outlooksByWeek.2: George Holani looks set as Seattle's No. 2 RB heading into a Week 2 matchup versus the Cardinals. Holani somewhat surprisingly logged eight carries in a tight Week 1 win over the Patriots, recording only two fewer totes than rookie Jadarian Price. However, Price was much more efficient with 5.2 YPC to Holani's 3.6. Price could get a larger share of the workload against the Cardinals, who limited the Chargers to 81 rushing yards on 21 carries in a season-opening victory.
outlooksByWeek.3: George Holani may be asked to take on a bigger offensive role for Seattle in a Week 3 matchup against the Commanders. Jadarian Price suffered a shoulder injury late in a Week 2 win against Arizona, and if he isn't able to suit up versus Washington, Holani would figure to see more work, though Emanuel Wilson would presumably take over No. 1 RB duties. As it is, Holani has gotten involved on offense in each of Seattle's contests so far, combining to produce 42 yards on 12 carries and two yards on one reception. The Commanders have been decimated through the air this season, but they haven't surrendered a rushing touchdown so far.

player.seasonOutlook: Holani is on the 2026 fantasy radar with Kenneth Walker III no longer on the Seattle roster and Zach Charbonnet (ACL) in doubt for the early portion of the season. Holani will compete with rookie Jadrian Price and Emanuel Wilson for touches while Charbonnet is sidelined. The 2024 UDFA has 25 carries and three targets to his name through two NFL seasons. Price figures to get the first shot at lead back duties and, even if forced into a few starts in Seattle's run-friendly offense, Holani would be working in a committee and no more than a deep league flex.

outlooksByWeek.2: Drew Lock is expected to serve as Seattle's starting quarterback in Week 2 versus Arizona due to Sam Darnold's glute injury. Lock took over in the first quarter of the Seahawks' season opener and guided the team to a win, completing 16 of 22 passes for 187 yards and one touchdown with no interceptions. Lock's TD was a 45-yard connection with Jaxon Smith-Njigba, who again figures to be his top target against the Cardinals. Arizona is coming off a surprising win against the Chargers, during which they limited Justin Herbert to 209 yards and an interception.
outlooksByWeek.3: Drew Lock could have another opportunity to lead Seattle's offense in Week 3 versus Washington. Lock started for the injured Sam Darnold (glute) on Sunday versus Arizona and threw for 235 yards with three touchdowns. Darnold is reportedly making good progress in his recovery, so it's not yet clear who will helm the team's offense in Week 3. Whichever QB gets the opportunity could be in for a big game against the Commanders, who have allowed a league-high seven passing touchdowns and have no interceptions through two weeks.

outlooksByWeek.2: Omar Cooper is uncertain to play for the Jets in Week 2 against the Packers due to an ankle sprain. In his NFL debut, he caught his only target for 30 yards. The Jets ran a heavy ground game to open the year, and while they will likely need to throw more in Week 2 to keep up, Cooper's role, even if healthy, is uncertain. The passing game should continue to flow heavily through Garrett Wilson, leaving Cooper's fantasy value volatile.

player.seasonOutlook: Cooper was selected by the Jets in the first round of April's draft. The Indiana product is fresh off a breakout 2025 season in which he posted a 69-937-13 receiving line after totaling 46 catches during his first three seasons with the Hoosiers. Primarily a perimeter target in limited action from 2022 to 2024, Cooper aligned in the slot on 80% of his routes last season. He is a short-area target (9.0 aDOT last season), but still posted strong efficiency numbers, including a 2.61 YPRR. He'll begin his career behind Garrett Wilson and Adonai Mitchell in New York's Geno Smith-led offense and is unlikely to produce consistent flex value as a rookie.

outlooksByWeek.3: Jameis Winston will take the reins of the Giants offense in Week 3 versus the Titans. Jaxson Dart suffered a serious knee injury and may not return this year. Winston's performance in relief of Dart last game left much to be desired, as he completed just 11-of-27 passes for 111 yards and an interception. Against Tennessee, at least Winston will have a week to prepare and face a lower-tier defense. The Titans are giving up 233.5 passing yards per game in 2026, which is 20th in the NFL.

player.seasonOutlook: Winston is back with the Giants and with Russell Wilson out of the picture, he is expected to serve as the primary backup to Jaxson Dart in 2026. Winston hasn't been a full-time starter since 2019 and was limited to two starts last season. In typical Winston style, results varied, with 11.0 fantasy points against Green Bay in Week 11, followed by a 32.2-point showing against Detroit the very next week. The 32-year-old doesn't do much with his legs, but his boom/bust passing style makes him an occasional streaming option when the matchup is right. That's what he'll be, if called on for a spot start in place of Dart this season.

outlooksByWeek.2: Tre' Harris had a quiet performance in the Chargers' season-opening loss to the Cardinals, catching three of six targets for 20 yards. The second-year wideout struggled along with the rest of the passing game under new offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel, with the exception of Ladd McConkey, and he was knocked out of the game in the third quarter with a rib injury. The injury doesn't appear to be serious, but if McConkey misses time, Harris could see additional volume. In Week 2, the second-year wideout will face a Raiders secondary that was tied for 21st in points allowed per game to WRs last season.
outlooksByWeek.3: Tre' Harris caught only one pass in the Chargers' Week 2 loss to the Raiders, but he made it count, connecting with a scrambling Justin Herbert for a 53-yard gain that set up a third-quarter touchdown. Harris has just a 4-73-0 line on nine targets through two games, but if he continues to show he can gain significant yards after the catch, he could prove to be a good fit for OC Mike McDaniel's scheme. The 2025 second-round pick will face a Bills secondary in Week 3 that's given up the fourth-most receiving yards to WRs so far this year.

player.seasonOutlook: Harris is a Year 2 breakout candidate after flashing in a limited role as a rookie. The 2025 second-round pick quietly played 49% of the Chargers' offensive snaps, but he spent a lot of that blocking and was limited to an 8% target share. Harris is likely to open the 2026 season behind Ladd McConkey and Quentin Johnston, but with Keenan Allen gone, his competition for No. 3 duties is 2025 fifth-round pick KeAndre Lambert-Smith and rookie Brenen Thompson. A potential starter in new playcaller Mike McDaniel's offense, the 24-year-old Harris is an intriguing late-round sleeper.

The Titans finished 25th in fantasy scoring from the D/ST last season, and other than draftees Dl Keldrick Faulk and LB Anthony Hill, didn't do much to substantially upgrade during the offseason. This looks like a one-and-done streamer, as the Titans face the Jets at home, a plus matchup, but are then a no-go in fantasy for the month that follows (PHI, @NYG, @BAL, HOU, @IND).

outlooksByWeek.2: David Njoku led the Chargers' tight end group in receiving during a season-opening loss to the Cardinals, catching all five of his targets for 58 yards. That far overshadowed Oronde Gadsden's two catches for 32 yards, while Charlie Kolar was predictably limited to blocking duties in new offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel's scheme. Top wideout Ladd McConkey did get knocked out of the game with a rib injury, however, and if he misses additional time, there could be more looks available for Njoku. He gets a potentially tough matchup in Week 2 against a Raiders defense that finished third in PPR points per game allowed to TEs last season.

player.seasonOutlook: Njoku signed with the Chargers after spending his first nine NFL seasons in Cleveland. The 2017 first-round pick was a late bloomer and has struggled with durability (he hasn't played a full season since 2018), but he has been a productive fantasy starter in recent years. Prior to a lost 2025 campaign, Njoku finished in the top eight among tight ends in fantasy PPG three seasons in a row. A force near the goal line, Njoku paced the position in end zone targets in both 2023 and 2024. At 30 years old, Njoku likely still has something left in the tank, but he has a tough path to fantasy relevance in a Los Angeles tight end room that also includes ascending Oronde Gadsden II and Charlie Kolar. Njoku will only be worth an add if he quickly takes control as the team's clear starter at the position.

outlooksByWeek.2: Ryan Flournoy managed two catches for 22 yards on four targets in the Week 1 loss for Dallas to the Giants. Flournoy finished fourth on the team in targets for the game. The Dallas passing attack struggled as a whole, leaving no receiver with more than 45 yards receiving in the contest. In Week 2, the Cowboys will look to rebound versus the Commanders. Washington only allowed 182 passing yards in its season opener, though did give up three passing scores to Philadelphia quarterback Jalen Hurts.
outlooksByWeek.3: Ryan Flournoy managed six targets last game for Dallas. Flournoy parlayed those looks into five catches for 23 yards. Flournoy was third in targets behind CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens. In Week 3, Dallas hosts the Baltimore Ravens. Baltimore is allowing just 191 passing yards per contest, which is 12th in the NFL.

player.seasonOutlook: Flournoy is an intriguing deep sleeper as the favorite for No. 3 wide receiver duties behind CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens in Dallas. Flournoy flashed in 2025, putting up 14.2 fantasy PPG during the only five games in which his route participation was at least 60%. Flournoy did disappear quite a bit behind the heavily targeted Lamb and Pickens (three or fewer targets in seven of his final 10 games), so he's a long shot for standalone fantasy value even if he locks down the No. 3 gig. The 26-year-old should be added to rosters only if Lamb or Pickens are sidelined.

outlooksByWeek.2: Pat Bryant was the Broncos' surprise target leader in their season-opening loss to Kansas City, catching four of six targets for 42 yards. Jaylen Waddle and Courtland Sutton were both taken out of the equation by the Chiefs secondary, forcing Bo Nix to look underneath for options like Bryant and tight end Evan Engram. Bryant had a solid finish to his rookie season in 2025, posting a 26-332-1 line on 39 targets over his final eight regular-season games, and his snap count and production suggest he's moved past Marvin Mims and Troy Franklin to take over the No. 3 wideout role for Denver. Bryant will look to stay involved in Week 2 against a Jaguars defense that was tied for 17th last season in points per game allowed to WRs.
outlooksByWeek.3: Pat Bryant fell back to earth after a promising season opener, failing to catch his only target in the Broncos' Week 2 win over the Jaguars. Quarterback Bo Nix made it a priority to get Jaylen Waddle going, and there wasn't much volume available for anyone else. Bryant gained 16 rushing yards on his only carry, but the No. 3 role in the Denver passing game doesn't figure to offer consistent production, and Bryant could face a challenge for the job once Marvin Mims overcomes a foot injury. Bryant will face a Rams secondary in Week 3 that's allowed just 19 receptions to WRs through two weeks, tied for seventh in the NFL, but three of them have gone for touchdowns.

player.seasonOutlook: A 2025 third-round pick, Bryant played a situational role throughout his rookie season and is likely to do the same in 2026 after Denver added Jaylen Waddle as a running mate for Courtland Sutton. Bryant will battle the likes of Troy Franklin, Marvin Mims Jr. and Lil'Jordan Humphrey for No. 3 duties. During his rookie campaign, Bryant barely saw the field early on, but eventually passed Franklin on the depth chart and earned more work down the stretch. That led to more snaps but not much fantasy production, as he failed to clear 13.2 fantasy points in a single game and found the end zone once. The 23-year-old isn't on the fantasy radar right now, but he makes for a fine dynasty stash.

outlooksByWeek.3: Marcus Mariota will likely start for the Commanders in Week 3, as starter Jayden Daniels dislocated the same elbow that he previously injured last season. Mariota relieved Daniels in the second half in Week 2 versus the Cowboys, throwing for 111 yards and a touchdown. He will have his work cut out for him versus a devastating Seattle defense that is allowing just 8.5 points and 214 scrimmage yards per game thus far in 2026, which is second in the league in both categories. Seattle is also allowing the fewest passing yards per contest at 124.5 per tilt.

outlooksByWeek.2: Chris Bell hopes for additional volume in the Dolphins Week 2 matchup at San Francisco. Coming off an ACL tear in November, the rookie logged a 52.7% snap share in his NFL debut, ending with a 25-yard catch on two targets. Malik Washington and Caleb Douglas dominated the targets in Miami's limited passing game, as expected given their availability throughout training camp. The 49ers' secondary doesn't appear to be one where Bell can break out, allowing just 6.4 yards per target in Week 1. Bell is worth monitoring, but he's currently off the fantasy radar.
outlooksByWeek.3: Chris Bell will look for a breakout opportunity in Week 3 when the Dolphins host the Chiefs. He has drawn only three targets through two weeks, resulting in one catch and a declining snap share, playing just 40% of offensive plays last week. A potential absence from Caleb Douglas (ankle) could elevate Bell to a WR2 role in a struggling offense that often throws while playing from behind. Kansas City's pass defense has been stingy, but should Douglas sit, Bell would be an intriguing high-upside option if chasing points in Week 3.

player.seasonOutlook: Bell was selected by the Dolphins in the third round of April's draft. The heaviest receiver in this rookie class at 222 pounds, Bell is a perimeter, possession target who increased his production in each of his four seasons at Louisville. That includes a 72-917-6 receiving line in 11 games last season, though he did tear his ACL in December. The injury could lead to a slow start to his NFL career, but considering he's joining a Miami offense devoid of playmakers, he also has a path to pacing the team in targets as a rookie. Bell could find his way to fantasy relevance if healthy and if Malik Willis plays well, but there are enough concerns that he's only worth a late flier.

outlooksByWeek.2: Carson Wentz could be in line to start again as the Vikings travel to Chicago in Week 2. Wentz came in for an injured Kyler Murray (concussion) against the Packers in Week 1, and he ended up delivering a come-from-behind win. The veteran completed 12 of 19 passes for 133 yards and three touchdowns, and he did not commit a turnover during the matchup. If Murray is unable to clear concussion protocol ahead of Sunday, Wentz will be in position to get his first start since 2025 against a Bears defense that gave up 361 passing yards, three touchdowns and one interception to Bryce Young in their opener.
outlooksByWeek.3: Carson Wentz will return to Minnesota's backup role in Week 3 against the Buccaneers. Wentz performed well while leading the Vikings to a 2-0 record, completing 23 of 39 passes for 276 yards and three touchdowns in that stretch. The veteran quarterback will remain a solid backup behind Kyler Murray, although anything can happen as the season progresses.

outlooksByWeek.2: Tyrone Tracy was the third-string running back in the season opener for the Giants while Najee Harris was a healthy scratch in Week 1, though that could change quickly. While Cam Skattebo and Devin Singletary look like the 1-2 duo out front, Tracy lost a fumble in the red zone that could have proven costly. Tracy had a rough camp even before the gaffe, so his time on the Giants could be coming to an end. If Tracy does suit up in Week 2, he will act mostly as depth against a Rams defense that was surprisingly suspect against the run in their first game of the season. The Rams allowed 174 yards on the ground, which currently ranks them 30th in the league. However, Aaron Donald will return to the fold out of retirement versus the G-Men.

player.seasonOutlook: Tracy is set to compete with Devin Singletary for opportunities in a Giants backfield led by second-year back Cam Skattebo. Tracy has produced 200-plus touches and 1,000-plus yards in each of his first two NFL seasons, but that doesn't tell the full story. Tracy got there as a fifth-round rookie in 2024 by impressing and taking New York's starting gig by Week 5. Last season, he quickly lost lead-back duties to Skattebo, but played a much larger role once Skattebo went down for the season with an injury (9.0 touches per game during Weeks 1-9, but 18.6 per game from Weeks 10-18). Tracy has no standalone fantasy value, but he's effective as a rusher and receiver. That makes the 26-year-old a solid backup who would be worth adding if Skattebo misses additional time.

outlooksByWeek.2: Zachariah Branch is expected to play a depth role in the Falcons' receiving room during the Week 2 matchup against the Panthers, whose defense allowed 9.0 yards per pass attempt in Week 1, which is tied for the fifth-worst mark in the NFL. Despite not receiving a target in his NFL debut, Branch tied Olamide Zaccheaus for the third-most snaps (18) amongst Falcons receivers. Additionally, he could be more involved in the Week 2 gameplan after Atlanta's offensive struggles last week. Even so, Branch is in for a great matchup against a Panthers defense that gave up eight total touchdowns in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Zachariah Branch is expected to play a depth role in Atlanta's WR room in the Week 3 matchup against the Packers. Branch played just 13 offensive snaps in the Week 2 loss to the Panthers -- which is five less than he logged in Week 1. It appears as if the rookie wideout's primary role is a return man, as he's operated as Atlanta's top punt returner this season. Branch's role could grow as the season progresses, but he's unlikely to find fantasy relevance in Week 3. Additionally, the Packers' defense has given up just 175 passing yards per game this season, making it an unfavorable matchup.

player.seasonOutlook: Branch was selected by the Falcons in the third round of April's draft. Branch is a tiny slot receiver who posted an extremely low 5.2 aDOT during 37 collegiate games. That limited his efficiency numbers a bit, though he caught 71% of his targets and was terrific after the catch (7.9 RAC). Branch has the look of a versatile (perhaps gadget) player who will help as a rusher, slot receiver and returner. That role makes him a longshot for consistent fantasy output, but he does have a path to No. 2 receiver duties behind Drake London with the likes of Olamide Zaccheaus and Jahan Dotson his primary competition. Branch should only be drafted in dynasty.

outlooksByWeek.2: Joshua Palmer's role within the Bills' offense is minimal at best entering a Week 2 matchup against the Lions. Palmer's snap share was 29% to open the season, and while his lone catch went for a big 34-yard gain, he drew just two targets. The passing game appears to flow through newly acquired DJ Moore, Khalil Shakir, and tight end Dalton Kincaid, keeping Palmer on the fringe for production despite a terrific matchup against a secondary that allowed 410 yards in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Joshua Palmer will look to make another chunk play for the Bills in Week 3 against the Chargers. Palmer has just two catches on the year, but they've gone for 34- and 43-yard touchdowns. The Chargers are allowing 10.8 yards per target to wideouts, the third highest through two weeks, so while volume isn't likely, Palmer could still contribute.

player.seasonOutlook: Conner is entering his 10th NFL season without a clear path to touches. For starters, we haven't seen him in a while after he suffered a season-ending foot injury in Week 3 last season. Even prior to the injury, Conner was splitting work with Trey Benson, totaling 28 touches in two full games. Conner restructured his contract during the offseason, but his days as Arizona's lead back are over after Jeremiyah Love and Tyler Allgeier were added to the roster during the offseason. Conner, who delivered four straight top-15 fantasy (points per game) campaigns prior to 2025, will need to find a new home in order to have any shot at 2026 fantasy relevance. He'll begin the season on IR.

Higgins is out for the 2026 season after tearing his ACL in mid August. As a rookie, the 2025 second-round pick played 58% of Houston's offensive snaps and handled a 12% target share en route to clearing 500 yards and scoring six touchdowns. Higgins averaged a lowly 7.6 fantasy PPG, but the 6-foot-4 perimeter receiver is a good bet for a larger role opposite Nico Collins once healthy in 2027. Keep him stashed in dynasty.

outlooksByWeek.2: Cade Otton will likely operate as one of the Buccaneers' top receiving options in the Week 2 matchup against the Browns. Otton caught just three of five targets for 26 yards in the Week 1 loss, but he was on the field for 56 of 57 offensive snaps, solidifying his role as Tampa Bay's top tight end. Additionally, Otton received the third-most targets on the Buccaneers, suggesting there's more production on the way. He's in for a favorable Week 2 matchup against a Browns defense that allowed 34 total points and 12.2 PPR fantasy points to TEs in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Cade Otton is expected to remain Tampa Bay's top tight end in the Week 3 matchup against the Vikings. Through two weeks, Otton is tied for the most targets (11) and second-most receptions (eight) on the Buccaneers, which is a good sign for his outlook moving forward. He's currently on pace to finish with career highs in targets (93) and receptions (68), though is role could diminish once Jalen McMillan returns to full speed. Otton is in for a difficult matchup in Week 3, as Minnesota's defense has allowed just 9.9 PPR fantasy points per game to TEs this season.

player.seasonOutlook: Otton re-signed with Tampa Bay after spending his first four NFL seasons with the team. Since entering the league in 2022, Otton ranks first among all tight ends in snaps (3,530) and second in routes (1,838). That simply hasn't translated to much target volume (he is yet to clear 86 in a season) or goal-line work (11 TDs and 19 end zone targets in 63 games). In fact, Otton was the only player with 75-plus targets who didn't score multiple touchdowns last season. The 27-year-old has finished 25th or lower in fantasy PPG in three of four seasons and is a poor bet for his first top-10 finish in 2026. He's well off the fantasy radar.

The first team to make it through a season without recording an interception since the category began being tracked in 1933, the Jets finished last in defensive fantasy scoring last season. Hey, they can only go up from here, right? Perhaps, but offseason additions of LB Demario Davis, S Minkah Fitzpatrick and LB David Bailey (the No. 2 overall pick in the draft) hardly vault this unit into the position's upper echelon. They do get a great matchup against the Titans in Week 1, though, so there's that?

Heidenreich was selected by the Steelers in the seventh round of April's draft. Heidenreich is an intriguing prospect, as he's a tweener who could play running back or receiver in the pros. The Navy product never cleared 77 carries in a single season, but did post a 51-941-6 receiving line in 2025. For his career, he averaged 6.85 yards per carry and evaded one tackle for every 5.9 touches, both of which are best in this RB rookie class. He'll likely max out as a gadget player behind Jaylen Warren and Rico Dowdle.

outlooksByWeek.2: Kendrick Bourne had a promising performance for Arizona in Week 1 and will look to be productive again versus the Seahawks in Week 2. Bourne led Cardinals wideouts with eight catches and 75 yards in a season-opening victory versus the Chargers, with only stud tight end Trey McBride outpacing his eight targets. The veteran Bourne looked to have great rapport with QB Jacoby Brissett, so it will be interesting to see how the target distribution shakes out in Week 2 and beyond. He won't have an easy matchup against Seattle, who limited New England to 178 yards through the air in a Week 1 win.
outlooksByWeek.3: Kendrick Bourne appears to have earned a key role in Arizona's passing game heading into a Week 3 matchup versus San Francisco. After joining the Cardinals in the offseason, Bourne has recorded 11 targets through two weeks, second-most among Arizona wide receivers. The veteran wideout has logged a 10-86-0 line on those opportunities, as he has established good chemistry with QB Jacoby Brissett. With that said, Week 3 could be another tough test for Arizona's air game: the 49ers have allowed just a 59.3 percent catch rate to WRs so far, ninth-best in the NFL.

outlooksByWeek.2: Odell Beckham earned a spot on the roster for the Giants, completing a remarkable comeback from injury. Though the nostalgia was high, Beckham did not even record a target in the season-opening win over the Cowboys in Week 1. With Malik Nabers now healthy, new additions Darnell Mooney and Malachi Fields ahead of him on the depth chart, and Isaiah Likely looking like a blossoming star at tight end, it will be difficult for Beckham to have much of an impact on the stat sheet this season. In Week 2, Odell and company will face a Rams defense that was surprisingly poor in its first game. Los Angeles gave up 205 passing yards and three touchdowns in a dismal loss in Australia to the 49ers, and also lost star pass rusher Myles Garrett to knee surgery.
outlooksByWeek.3: Odell Beckham has yet to catch a pass through two games for the Giants. The bigger news may be that starting quarterback Jaxson Dart could be lost for the season due to a knee injury. With Jameis Winston under center, Beckham will likely see his stock further take a hit. In Week 3, the Giants will face a lackluster Titans defense allowing 233.5 passing yards per clash, which is 20th in the league, though Beckham looks more like depth than anything else at this point.

outlooksByWeek.2: DeMario Douglas will seek more production in Week 2 when the Patriots face the Steelers. He logged a reasonable seven targets to open the season but turned that into just 20 yards on five grabs. Douglas has a rapport with QB Drake Maye as a safety valve, and while snaps seem safe with A.J. Brown (ankle) sidelined for the foreseeable future, Douglas topped 40 yards just four times last season.
outlooksByWeek.3: DeMario Douglas' role in New England's struggling passing offense is questionable ahead of a Week 3 game at Jacksonville. In Week 2, Douglas logged just two targets in his first full game without A.J. Brown after a seven-target opener, and he's averaging just 4.8 yards per reception to start the season. Jacksonville is allowing a hefty 10.3 yards per target to opposing wideouts, but Douglas' inability to stretch the field would require uncharacteristic heavy volume to provide a modest fantasy return.

player.seasonOutlook: Pearsall (knee) is out for the 2026 season after battling injuries during his first two NFL campaigns. The 2024 first-round pick's rookie season ended on a strong note (18-plus fantasy points in Weeks 17 and 18) and that momentum carried over early in 2025 (14.6 fantasy PPG during Weeks 1-3). Pearsall then suffered a knee injury and went on to average 7.5 PPG in six games the rest of the season. Pearsall holds the unfortunate distinction of having the most targets among all players who failed to score a single TD last season. Pearsall will enter 2027 - his age-27 campaign - eyeing his first fully healthy campaign and will battle for a starting job in San Francisco. He's no longer a must hold in dynasty, but he's a fine enough hold in deep leagues.

outlooksByWeek.2: Andy Borregales hopes his scoring chances will elevate with a bounce-back offensive performance from the Patriots in Week 2 against the Steelers. Borregales had only two opportunities as the team struggled to move the ball in Seattle, and unfortunately, Week 2's game doesn't profile as high-scoring. Perhaps that increases Borregales' three-point opportunities, and he's a reliable option from all over the field. Pittsburgh allowed four field-goal attempts last week.
outlooksByWeek.3: Andy Borregales' opportunities could again be limited when the Patriots face the Jaguars in Week 3. Borregales missed his first kick of the season in Week 2, and through two games, has just four field-goal attempts and three extra points as New England's offense has struggled to sustain drives. Jacksonville has allowed just three field goals and three extra points through two games, so there are likely more reliable Week 3 options.

outlooksByWeek.2: Demarcus Robinson should again have a key role for San Francisco in Week 2 against the Dolphins. After rookie De'Zhaun Stribling hurt his ankle in a season-opening win over the Rams, Robinson stepped up as the team's No. 3 wideout and produced two catches for 50 yards and a touchdown. Stribling is expected to miss at least a month, so Robinson will likely continue to work as the 49ers third wideout behind Mike Evans and Deebo Samuel. Miami presents a good matchup after falling to the Raiders 27-13 and yielding three passing touchdowns Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Demarcus Robinson suffered an ankle injury in San Francisco's win over the Dolphins on Sunday, and his status is very much in doubt for a Week 3 matchup against Arizona. Before getting hurt, Robinson caught all three of his targets for 34 yards against Miami as the 49ers' No. 3 wideout. In the likely scenario that he can't play in Week 3, Jacob Cowing would stand to step into Robinson's place in the pecking order. Arizona has given up four receiving TDs to wide receivers through two weeks, tied for the most in the league.

outlooksByWeek.2: Dominic Zvada connected on all four of his kicks in Week 1 for the Giants. Zvada made all four of his PATs during the 28-20 win for the G-Men over the Dallas Cowboys. He did not attempt a field goal for the game. In Week 2, Zvada and company will face a Rams squad that was surprisingly suspect in its season opener. Los Angeles allowed 27 points to the 49ers in a losing effort last week.
outlooksByWeek.3: Dominic Zvada accounted for the only points for the Giants last game. Zvada connected on both of his field goals in the 28-6 loss to the Rams. The injury to Jaxson Dart leaves Jameis Winston under center at quarterback, which could be an ugly development in terms of opportunities for points for Zvada. In Week 3, the Giants will face a Titans squad allowing 23.5 points per tilt, which is tied for 16th in the NFL.

outlooksByWeek.2: Greg Dulcich will look for increased target share in Week 2 when the Dolphins face the 49ers. Entering the season opener, Miami had minimal proven pass catchers, creating optimism around Dulcich, but despite a 74% snap rate, Dulcich was targeted just twice. San Francisco allowed just four catches and 31 yards to tight ends in their opener, so even if Miami is forced to throw from behind, it doesn't yet appear Dulcich has Malik Willis' eye, suggesting there are better fantasy options.
