He was effective prior to the injury, averaging 5.5 yards per carry, and was busy as a receiver (four-plus targets in three straight games). The 24-year-old will open the 2026 season on injured reserve and, even when healthy, he's no longer assured of a role with a new coaching staff and after the team added Jeremiyah Love and Tyler Allgeier. Benson's best days are likely ahead of him, but his only shot at 2026 fantasy relevance is a new home or several injuries above him on the Arizona depth chart.

Sanders is back as a pass-catching tight end in Carolina, though he's unlikely to see a larger share of the target pie with veteran Darren Waller now in the mix. Sanders - a 2024 fourth-round pick - flashed as a rookie with a 33-342-1 receiving line while playing 55% of Carolina's offensive snaps and handling 9.1% of the targets across 16 games. He simply didn't progress in Year 2, posting a 29-190-1 line while playing 52% of the snaps and handling a 10% target share in 12 healthy games. Sanders has been an inefficient short-range target with little goal line activity thus far (four career end zone targets), placing the 23-year-old well off the fantasy radar.

outlooksByWeek.2: Devontez Walker and the Ravens face the Saints and their 21st-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed per game (37.2) to WRs in Week 2. Walker, who has seven catches for 157 yards and four TDs across two seasons with Baltimore, sat out the Week 1 victory with a groin injury. Keep an eye on his status in practice leading up to their clash with New Orleans, as the Ravens are pretty banged up at receiver. Zay Flowers (hamstring) is considered day-to-day while rookie Ja'Kobi Lane (wrist) is doubtful, meaning Walker could have a chance to make some noise if he suits up in Week 2.
outlooksByWeek.3: Devontez Walker and the Ravens travel to take on the Cowboys in Week 3. The third-year receiver hauled in one of two targets for 47 yards in Baltimore's Week 2 loss, good for third on the team in receiving yards. Rashod Bateman (7-88-1) filled in admirably for Zay Flowers, who sat out with a hamstring injury, but there's a high chance of the latter making his return to the field in Week 3. Walker's fantasy upside remains limited in a run-heavy offense, however, despite a potential shootout in Dallas.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jahdae Walker will aim to stay involved as the Bears play the Vikings in Week 2. Walker made a mark in Chicago's season-opener win over the Panthers with his limited opportunities, reeling in his one catch for a one-yard touchdown. The second-year wide receiver could continue to see success this season, especially if the Bears continue to score at such a high rate. He'll face a Minnesota defense that allowed two touchdowns to Packers WRs in Week 1.

Barion Brown will likely have minimal offensive impact in the Saints' Week 2 matchup against the Ravens. Brown played just seven offensive snaps in his NFL debut, suggesting he's clearly behind fellow rookie Bryce Lance (62 snaps) in the Saints' receiving corps. With Tyler Shough attempting 56 passes in the Week 1 loss, it's tough to imagine a better scenario for Brown to make an impact as well. It'll be a tough Week 2 matchup against a Ravens defense that's given up just 25.0 PPR fantasy points to wideouts this season.
outlooksByWeek.3: Barion Brown is expected to play a depth role in the Saints' receiving corps in the Week 3 matchup against the Raiders. Brown has logged just nine offensive snaps through New Orleans' first two games, suggesting he's not a part of head coach Kellen Moore's offensive game plan. It appears as if the rookie's primary role is in the return game, as he's accumulated 34 punt-return yards and 128 kick-return yards already. Additionally, Brown is in for a difficult Week 3 matchup against a Raiders defense that's allowed just 6.8 yards per pass attempt thus far.

player.seasonOutlook: Brown was selected by the Saints in the sixth round of April's draft. Brown is a thin, vertical receiver who handled a healthy 21% target share across 50 collegiate games at Kentucky and LSU. Brown struggled a bit with drops and efficiency, but made some noise as a rusher (32-228-2 across four seasons) and figures to make his biggest impact as a kick returner (65 kick returns for 1,910 yards and six TDs are all easily tops in this rookie class). With Chris Olave, Devaughn Vele and Jordyn Tyson (once healthy) cemented atop the depth chart, Brown is well off the fantasy radar.

Richardson enters his fourth NFL season as a backup to Daniel Jones. Last season, Richardson played just 14 snaps off the bench and missed most of the season with an eye injury. If ever called on to start, Richardson will be an interesting fantasy wild card. On one hand, the 2023 fourth-overall pick has a ton of upside; he ranked no lower than sixth among QBs in carries, rushing yards and rush TDs in 2024 despite only playing 10 full games, while also pacing the position in average depth of throw and yards per completion. That led to four 20-plus fantasy point games. On the other hand, Richardson's poor passing may lead to many duds. He had fewer than 15 fantasy points in his other six outings, threw 12 INTs on the season (fourth most) and his 48% completion percentage ranked last. In total, he averaged 15.8 fantasy PPG in the 10 games, which would've ranked 15th over the full season. Richardson's elite rushing ability and aggressive passing style are the only reason to keep him stashed in deep dynasty leagues.

outlooksByWeek.3: Darius Cooper caught the game-winning touchdown for the Eagles in Week 2. Cooper managed just two catches for 26 yards, though one of them gave the Eagles the lead for good with precious seconds left on the clock. Cooper also tied for third on the team in targets for the game. In Week 3, Philadelphia will face a Bears defense allowing 240 passing yards per tilt thus far this season, which is 25th in the NFL. The Eagles could also rely even more on the passing game if Saquon Barkley is sidelined due to injury.

outlooksByWeek.2: Brock Wright could continue to carve out a role for himself as the Lions travel to Buffalo in Week 2. There wasn't a lot of hype around Wright heading into the 2026 campaign, but the sixth-year tight end was on the field for nearly 50 percent of offensive snaps and reeled in his sole target for five yards. The veteran could be in store for more opportunities moving forward, and with the volatility of Sam LaPorta injury-wise, Wright is someone to keep on the radar. He'll face a Bills defense that ceded 14.4 PPR points to Texans tight ends this past Sunday.
outlooksByWeek.3: Brock Wright remains a depth option as the Lions play the Jets in Week 3. Wright remained on the field for a good number of snaps (26 percent) in Week 2, but the TE2 was unable to garner a target. The sixth-year tight end will need to run more routes before he can be trusted as anything more than a blocker. He'll also face a New York defense that ranks third in fantasy points per game allowed to tight ends so far this campaign.

player.seasonOutlook: Benson was selected by the Raiders in the sixth round of April's draft. An accomplished sprinter, the speedy Benson has big play written all over him, though he's a slightly older prospect and his collegiate production was limited by a lot of changes in scenery (two years of community college followed by 2023 at Alabama, 2024 at Florida State and 2025 at Oregon). Benson never cleared a 15% target share in a single season, peaking with a 43-719-6 receiving line in 2025. Benson is a longshot as a sixth rounder, but the Raiders' shaky wide receiver depth chart presents him with an opportunity to quickly earn a role. Still, he's no more than a deep sleeper.

outlooksByWeek.2: Josh Oliver will seek to stay involved in Minnesota's passing game at Chicago in Week 2. Oliver was an unlikely contributor against the Packers in Week 1, logging two catches for 22 yards and ranking third on the team in targets (four). With veteran Carson Wentz also very likely to serve under center once again, the seventh-year tight end could be in line for more targets. He'll face a Bears defense that allowed a middle-of-the-pack 11.5 PPR points to Panthers tight ends in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Josh Oliver will aim to stay involved in Minnesota's passing game against Tampa Bay in Week 3. Oliver stayed active in a low-scoring Week 2 win against the Bears, reeling in his sole target for a 24-yard gain. The supplementary tight end has now amassed three catches for 46 yards off five targets in his first two outings. He'll take on a New York defense that's allowed a third-lowest 6.0 PPR points per game to TEs so far this season.

outlooksByWeek.2: Isaiah Bond and the Browns are in Tampa Bay to clash with the Buccaneers in Week 2. Although healthy and active for the season opener after clearing concussion protocol, Bond played just seven offensive snaps and didn't see any time on special teams. Cleveland's offense was not very good in its first appearance, and as long as questions remain at the quarterback position, there's no reason to trust any of their pass-catchers until proven otherwise.
outlooksByWeek.3: Isaiah Bond and the Browns welcome the Panthers to town for a Week 3 tilt. He caught his lone target for 10 yards during Cleveland's shocking victory over Tampa Bay in Week 2. It appears rookie receivers Denzel Boston (5-95-1) and KC Concepcion (6-28-0), along with tight end Harold Fannin Jr. (5-54-0), will be the focal point of the passing game, leaving Bond and Jerry Jeudy as the odd men out. Bond can be left on waiver wires in all formats versus a Panthers defense allowing 30.3 fantasy points (T-15th) to WRs.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jordan Whittington will look to improve upon a quiet season opener when the Rams face the Giants in Week 2. Whittington had just one catch for eight yards in Week 1 versus San Francisco. Still, he was the only Rams WR outside of stars Puka Nacua and Davante Adams to log a reception. Nacua and Adams stand to command most of QB Matthew Stafford's attention, so Whittington figures to compete for scraps with Los Angeles' tight ends and other depth wideouts each week. The Giants held Dallas' passing game in check in Week 1, as QB Dak Prescott tallied just 175 yards through the air, though he did toss two TDs.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jordan Whittington (quadriceps) sat out the Rams' Week 2 win over the Giants and isn't certain to return for a Week 3 matchup against Denver. It was a missed opportunity Monday for Whittington, as top wideout Puka Nacua (hip) was also sidelined, opening the door for other WRs to take on a bigger role. Whittington was quiet in Week 1 against San Francisco with just one catch on one target for eight yards, and when both Nacua and Davante Adams are healthy, he figures to be competing with a variety of other pass catchers for targets. Should Whittington return in Week 3, he'll draw a tough Broncos secondary that has allowed a 51.6 percent catch rate to wideouts -- second best in the league -- so far this season.

outlooksByWeek.2: Colbie Young and the Bengals are in Houston for a Week 2 tilt against the Texans. The rookie fourth-round pick played just nine offensive snaps and did not record a target during Cincinnati's season-opening win. As long as Ja'Marr Chase, Tee Higgins, Chase Brown, and Mike Gesicki are all healthy, Young's time on the field and opportunities will remain limited.
outlooksByWeek.3: Colbie Young and the Bengals travel to face the Steelers in Week 3. The rookie fourth-rounder caught his only target for seven yards during Cincinnati's Week 2 win over Houston, giving him his first career reception in his second game. Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins accounted for 19 of Joe Burrow's 31 pass attempts, so Young remains firmly off the fantasy radar. In Week 3, he'll face a Steelers defense that ranks second, allowing just 15.5 fantasy points per game to WRs so far in 2026.

outlooksByWeek.2: Brenen Thompson was on the field for just 10 offensive snaps in his NFL debut and failed to get a target in the Chargers' season-opening loss to the Cardinals. The fourth-round speedster could still end up being useful in new offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel's scheme, but the whole unit is still adjusting. Top wideout Ladd McConkey left the game early with a rib injury, and if he misses additional time, it could open the door for Thompson to take on a bigger role, although he would still likely be behind Quentin Johnston and Tre' Harris in the pecking order. In Week 2, Thompson will face a Raiders secondary that was tied for 21st in points per game allowed to WRs last season.
outlooksByWeek.3: Brenen Thompson began to work into the offense a little more in Week 2, notching his first three targets and catching one of them for 13 yards. That usage may have been due to Ladd McConkey nursing a rib injury, but Thompson's elite speed could earn a consistent spot in OC Mike McDaniel's quick-strike game plan if he shows he can get open against NFL defenders. Thompson will try to keep building chemistry with QB Justin Herbert in Week 3 against a Bills secondary that's given up the fourth-most receiving yards to WRs this year.

player.seasonOutlook: Thompson was selected by the Chargers in the fourth round of April's draft. Thompson is an extremely small and very fast (4.26 40-yard dash) receiver who posted a rookie-class-high 18.5 YPR during his career and handled a massive 43% of Mississippi State's air yards last season. He didn't see much work prior to 2025, however, and figures to operate as a situational deep threat in the pros. He'll battle second-years Tre Harris and KeAndre Lamber-Smith for occasional looks behind Ladd McConkey and Quentin Johnston this season.

Klare was selected by the Rams in the second round of April's draft. Klare is a receiving tight end who has experience playing in line and in the slot. He might not offer much as a blocker in the pros, but he showed his receiving ability at two different schools, posting a 51-685-4 line with Purdue in 2024 and a 43-448-2 line with Ohio State in 2025. Klare has the speed and athleticism to eventually emerge as a fantasy option, but hell begin his career in a crowded tight end room that also includes Colby Parkinson, Tyler Higbee, Davis Allen and 2025 second-round pick Terrance Ferguson. Klare is nowhere close to fantasy relevance at the moment.

Brazzell was selected by the Panthers in the third round of April's draft. He's expected to miss his rookie season due to a knee injury suffered in July. Brazzell is a tall, perimeter receiver with a big wingspan who will do most of his damage down field (career 14.2 aDOT at Tennessee) and doesn't offer much after the catch (3.6 RAC was worst in this rookie WR class). He has good speed (4.37 40-yard dash) and may settle in as a boom/bust low-volume, splash-play fantasy option. He'll battle for a starting role behind Tetairoa McMillan in 2027.

outlooksByWeek.2: Dyami Brown saw two targets in Week 1 for the Commanders. Unfortunately, he could not corral either target and went catchless in the opener. Meanwhile, rookie Antonio Williams looks to have cemented himself as the No. 3 wideout behind Scary Terry and Stefon Diggs with four catches for 64 yards and a touchdown to lead Washington. That being said, there could be plenty of ball to go around in Week 2 versus a Dallas defense that looked dreadful all of last season, as well as Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Dyami Brown tied for second on the Commanders last game with six targets. That led to four catches for 21 yards in the 37-20 loss to Dallas. Unfortunately, starting quarterback Jayden Daniels only played a half due to injury, so veteran backup Marcus Mariota will likely start in Week 3 versus a devastating Seattle defense. The Seahawks are allowing just 8.5 points per game thus far in 2026, which is second in the league. Seattle is also allowing the fewest passing yards per contest at 124.5 per tilt. None of this appears to be a recipe for success for Brown and the rest of the Washington offense.

outlooksByWeek.2: Bo Melton should remain a secondary option as the Packers take on the Jets in Week 2. Melton was a solid returner in Week 1 against the Vikings, but he also recorded a pivotal 10-yard first-down catch in the matchup. This makes it evident that while small, the fourth-year playmaker's role on offense is not gone. He'll aim to stay involved against a Jets defense that allowed a middle-of-the-pack 30.5 PPR points per game against wide receivers in 2025.
outlooksByWeek.3: Bo Melton will aim to get involved as the Packers play the Falcons in Week 3. Melton was unable to reel in his sole target in Week 2 against the Jets, but he did get an uptick in usage after Jayden Reed went down with an injury. Melton could be in line for more looks, especially if Reed misses a lot of time. He'll face an Atlanta defense that's allowed a middle-of-the-pack 30.3 PPR points per game to WRs so far this season.

Jalen Royals scored his first career NFL touchdown in Kansas City's Week 2 overtime win over the Colts, snagging a one-yard toss from Patrick Mahomes in the third quarter-the third of three TD passes for the superstar QB on the night. Royals, a fourth-round pick in 2025, has only four career catches in nine regular-season games, and he's firmly behind Rashee Rice, Xavier Worthy, and Tyquan Thornton on the WR depth chart. With Mahomes spreading the ball around early in the season, Royals could begin to establish a small but consistent role in the passing game. He'll face a Dolphins defense in Week 3 that's given up five passing TDs through two games but only one to a wide receiver.

player.seasonOutlook: Klubnik was selected by the Jets in the fourth round of April's draft. Klubnik is an undersized, conservative quarterback who ranked last in this rookie class in aDOT (7.4), yards per completion (11.1), yards per attempt (7.1) and QB rating (136) during his collegiate tenure. He peaked with a 36-to-6 TD-to-INT showing in 2024, but fell to 16 TDs and six INTs in 2025. Klubnik does have a lot of experience (three years as a starter at Clemson) and could add value with his legs (totaled a 294-1,429-17 rushing line in his career), though he was extremely inefficient in the latter in 2025. Klubnik will handle No. 2 duties behind Geno Smith, but could handle some starts later in the year.

outlooksByWeek.2: Olamide Zaccheaus is in for a very favorable Week 2 matchup when the Falcons take on the Panthers. Carolina is coming off one of the worst defensive performances in recent memory, allowing 59 points in a Week 1 loss to the Bears. Despite Zaccheaus playing just 18 offensive snaps and catching his lone target last week, he could find value in this incredible matchup. Zaccheaus' value could depend on which quarterback starts for Atlanta as well, with both Michael Penix (knee) and Tua Tagovailoa (oblique) battling injuries.
outlooksByWeek.3: Olamide Zaccheaus is expected to play a depth role in the Falcons' receiving corps during the Week 3 matchup against the Packers. Zaccheaus played 29 offensive snaps in the Week 2 loss to the Panthers -- which is 11 more than he did in Week 1. However, this didn't lead to an increase in production, as he caught just one of three targets for three yards. Zaccheaus could benefit from the return of quarterback Michael Penix in Week 3, but he'll likely have to find the end zone to be fantasy relevant. Additionally, he could struggle against a Packers defense that's given up just 5.4 yards per pass attempt this season, the fifth-best mark in the NFL.

player.seasonOutlook: Delp was selected by the Saints in the third round of April's draft. Delp was busy during his final three seasons at Georgia (1,733 snaps in 42 games), but that didn't lead to much work in the passing game (no more than 24 catches, 284 yards or a 7% target share in a single season). Good speed and hands suggest there's some hope for him as a developmental piece, which is what he'll be in 2026 while playing a situational role behind Juwan Johnson and Noah Fant.

outlooksByWeek.3: Johnny Mundt caught two passes in Dallas Goedert's place last game for the Eagles, and would be the next man up at tight end if Goedert cannot suit up in Week 3. Goedert suffered a knee injury last game for Philadelphia and did not return, leaving his status in question for the clash with Chicago. Goedert is set to undergo testing to determine the nature and extent of the issue. In Week 3, Philadelphia will face a Bears defense allowing 240 passing yards per tilt thus far this season, which is 25th in the NFL.

player.seasonOutlook: Roush was selected by the Bears in the third round of April's draft. Roush is a huge, in-line blocking tight end. Though he did catch 40-plus passes each of his final two seasons at Stanford (including a healthy 22% target share in 2025), his overall receiving efficiency was underwhelming (6.6 YPT, 1.22 YPRR) and he totaled four TDs on 182 career targets. He's unlikely to see enough target volume in the pros to find his way to the fantasy radar and that's especially the case in Chicago, as he's buried behind Colston Loveland and Cole Kmet.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jimmy Horn will likely play a minimal offensive role in the Panthers' Week 2 matchup against the Falcons, whose defense allowed just 22.4 PPR fantasy points to wideouts in Week 1. Horn had a poor Week 1 performance despite not receiving an offensive touch, as the second-year wideout had a costly fumble on a punt return that helped set up a Bears touchdown. He's not expected to see much volume or be very involved in Carolina's offensive game plan going forward, especially with the emergence of Jalen Coker (ankle). Horn is also in for a tough divisional matchup in Week 2, with the Falcons' defense allowing just 6.5 yards per target to WRs last week.

LaJohntay Wester and the Ravens host the Saints in Week 2. The second-year receiver played 19 of 68 offensive snaps in the season-opening victory, hauling in both of his targets for 15 yards. He also worked on special teams, but with Zay Flowers (hamstring), Ja'Kobi Lane (wrist), and Devontez Walker (groin) all either questionable or doubtful to play in Week 2, more opportunities open up. New Orleans surrendered 206 yards and two TDs through the air in its Week 1 loss to Detroit.

Tai Felton will look to get more chances in Minnesota's passing game against Chicago in Week 2. Felton garnered zero targets in a Week 1 win over the Packers, but he was on the field with the offense, which could contribute to some looks in the coming weeks. Veteran Carson Wentz played under center for most of the game, and Vikings receivers Jordan Addison and Jauan Jennings both did not record a catch. Given that Wentz could serve as the quarterback again, Felton could fill a niche in the passing game behind Justin Jefferson and T.J. Hockenson. The Bears defense also allowed the fourth-most PPR points to wide receivers (46.3) in Week 1, which could open up Minnesota's passing game even more.

player.seasonOutlook: Klein was selected by the Texans in the second round of April's draft. He's an inexperienced, blocking tight end who posted an ugly 5.5 YPT and 57.6% catch rate in his collegiate career. Klein peaked with a 24-248-1 receiving line in 2025 and now joins a Texans' offense that already includes Dalton Schultz, Cade Stover and Foster Moreau at the tight end position. Klein may be Houston's tight end of the future, but he won't be on the fantasy radar as a rookie.

Daniels was selected by the Rams in the sixth round of April's draft. It helped that he played in 68 games across six seasons at Liberty, LSU and Miami, but Daniels ranked third in this WR rookie class in receiving yards (2,991) and second in TD receptions (28) for his career. His overall efficiency was good, though he failed to emerge as anything more than a secondary target once he left Liberty. Daniels will battle for a roster spot and is no more than a dynasty stash.

outlooksByWeek.3: Jacob Cowing stands to take on a bigger role in San Francisco's offense if Demarcus Robinson (ankle) can't suit up versus Arizona in Week 3. Cowing hasn't seen much opportunity on offense yet, playing just 27 offensive snaps without drawing a target through two games. However, Robinson seems likely to miss Week 3 due to his injury, and if that's the case Cowing would likely be called upon to step into a larger amount of work in the passing game. The Cardinals haven't been good against the pass this season and just allowed star Seattle WR Jaxon Smith-Njigba to rack up 155 receiving yards and three TDs in Week 2.

player.seasonOutlook: Cameron was selected by the Jaguars in the sixth round of April's draft. Cameron is a big, strong, perimeter receiver who aligned out wide on 84% of his collegiate routes across five seasons at Baylor. Cameron's overall efficiency is underwhelming (1.58 YPRR), but he was certainly busy the last two seasons, totaling 52-754-10 and 69-872-9 receiving lines. He'll begin his career no higher than fifth on the Jacksonville depth chart behind Brian Thomas Jr., Jakobi Meyers, Parker Washington and Travis Hunter.

Nowakowski was selected by the Steelers in the fifth round of April's draft. Nowakowski is a bit undersized with very small hands, but he's a capable blocker and, after totaling 18 catches in 36 games at Wisconsin, made a little bit of a leap as a pass catcher in 2025 (his lone season at Indiana), posting a 32-387-2 receiving line. He's expected to play fullback and offer some tight end depth behind Pat Freiermuth and Darnell Washington.

Kacmarek was selected by the Dolphins in the third round of April's draft. Kacmarek is a massive, strong blocking tight end who won't see much receiving work in the pros. He's likely to play a lot of snap as a rookie considering Miami's shaky roster, but Greg Dulcich is expected to operate as the team's top pass-catcher at the tight end position. Kacmarek is no more than the deepest of deep sleepers.

Boerkircher was selected by the Jaguars in the second round of April's draft. Boerkircher is a blocking tight end who handled a 3% target share (lowest in this rookie TE class) across 52 collegiate games (five seasons). He aligned in the slot 30% of the time and posted a 1.04 YPRR, both of which are lowest in this TE group. He'll file in as a blocking complement to starter Brenton Strange and is not a fantasy option.

Rudolph is expected to return as the clipboard holder in Pittsburgh, with Aaron Rodgers back as the starter. The veteran quarterback has never appeared in more than 10 games in a single season and made just one start in 2025 (he threw for 171 yards and one TD on 31 attempts). Rudolph has thrown 30 touchdowns and 22 interceptions in his six-year career, and isn't much of a rushing threat (career 75-209-1). The 31-year-old wouldn't even be a QB2 option in superflex if called on to start.

Green was selected by the Browns in the sixth round of April's draft. Green is a huge, aggressive dual-threat quarterback. He's a major threat with his legs (112-999-8 rushing last season) but a work in progress as a passer, as he completed only 61% of his passes and threw 11 INTs on only 326 attempts in 2025. Green's size and athleticism (which included a 4.36 40-yard dash at the combine) supplies him with massive upside, but he'll need to improve as a passer in order to find a starting opportunity. He'll continue to compete for playing time with Deshaun Watson, Shedeur Sanders and Dillon Gabriel.

Leonard is expected to operate as the Colts' No. 2 quarterback this season. It's a notable designation, as starter Daniel Jones continues to recover from a torn Achilles suffered in Week 14 last season. Should Jones miss time to begin the 2026 season, Leonard is positioned to start. Leonard made one start as a rookie, throwing for 270 yards and two touchdowns and rushing for 21 yards and an additional score, primarily against Houston's backup defense in Week 18. The 2025 sixth-round pick adds value with his legs, but he'd be no more than a fringe QB2 even if called on to start.
Shavers tore his ACL in the playoffs and is unlikely to make a fantasy impact once back on the field in 2026.

Joly was selected by the Broncos in the fifth round of April's draft, but was later waived and claimed by Miami. Joly is a highly productive receiving tight end who ranked near the top of this rookie TE class in all receiving counting stats (166-1,978-15) and target share (17%) during 50 collegiate games at UConn and NC State. He's not much of a blocker, but he could stretch the seam as a move tight end in the pros. Joly may one day emerge as a receiving option, but it's going to take some time.

Miller was selected by the Patriots in the seventh round of April's draft. Miller has decent size, but he has struggled with effectiveness, posting a 4.57 YPC (worst in this rookie class) during his collegiate career (including an ugly 3.88 in 2025). Poor tackle breaking and YAC numbers give him perhaps the worst efficiency profile in this RB class, and he hasn't shown much in the passing game (career 40-336-2 line). He ran a solid 4.42 40-yard dash at the combine but posted the worst marks in this RB class in the vertical and broad jump. He didn't make the initial 53-man roster, but will look to stick on the practice squad.

Cuevas was selected by the Ravens in the fifth round of April's draft. Cuevas wasn't targeted much during three collegiate seasons at Washington and Alabama (57-793-6, 5% target share), but he was effective when called on, averaging 10.4 yards per target. He's a bit of a tweener and underwhelmed athletically at the combine, but can help as a blocker and receiver. He'll battle fellow rookie Matthew Hibner for snaps behind Mark Andrews and Durham Smythe this season.

outlooksByWeek.3: Brycen Tremayne is expected to play a reserve role in the Panthers' receiving corps in the Week 3 matchup against the Browns. Tremayne was thought to have a larger role in the Panthers' offensive game plan heading into Week 2, as the team cut ties with Jimmy Horn. However, Tremayne played just nine offensive snaps and didn't receive a target, as his role remains primarily on special teams. The third-year wideout is in for a favorable matchup, however, with the Browns' defense allowing four touchdowns to WRs through two contests.

player.seasonOutlook: Nussmeier was selected by the Chiefs in the seventh round of April's draft. Nussmeier is an undersized, pocket quarterback and older prospect. He was extremely conservative last season, posting rookie-class-low marks in aDOT (6.4), YPA (6.7) and YPC (9.9). Aside of his ability to avoid sacks (career 3.40% sack rate), Nussmeier's efficiency isn't overly impressive and he's a nonfactor as a rusher (career 33-179-5 line and a class-low 1.4 carries per game). Nussmeier will handle No. 3 duties behind Patrick Mahomes and Justin Fields.

outlooksByWeek.3: Jared Wayne drew seven targets in Week 2 as the Texans played without top WR Nico Collins (hamstring). Wayne could be an option for desperate deep-league fantasy managers in Week 3 against a Colts defense that has allowed the most points and yards in the league. If Collins sits again, Wayne will join Xavier Hutchinson, Kayshon Boutte, and Jaylin Noel as the only healthy options in Houston's WR room. Wayne caught only two of his seven targets in Week 2 against the Bengals, and he has only 65 career receiving yards in six games across three seasons in Houston.

outlooksByWeek.2: Jalen Brooks was a non-factor for Arizona in Week 1, but he'll look to make an impact versus Seattle in Week 2. Brooks logged just four offensive snaps in the season-opener versus the Chargers and didn't draw any targets. It didn't help his case for a larger role that newcomer Kendrick Bourne played well with eight catches on eight targets for 75 yards as the No. 3 wideout on the depth chart. All of Arizona's pass catchers face a tough challenge against a Seahawks squad that is expected to have one of the league's best defenses again in 2026.
outlooksByWeek.3: Jalen Brooks has yet to get going this season heading into Arizona's Week 3 clash with San Francisco. Brooks hasn't yet drawn a target, but that's partly because he's logged just six offensive snaps through two weeks. Among Cardinals wideouts, only Michael Wilson, Marvin Harrison Jr. and Kendrick Bourne have recorded receptions so far, and it remains to be seen if the team will eventually look to get its other WRs involved. San Francisco has been strong against the pass through two weeks, ranking in the top 10 in most categories versus wide receivers.

player.seasonOutlook: Virgil was selected by the Cardinals in the fifth round of April's draft. Virgil is a tall, thin, perimeter, vertical receiver who ranked near the top of this WR rookie class in aDOT (14.7) and YPR (15.8) but near the basement in RAC (4.5), catch rate (54%) and YPRR (1.79) during his career at Miami Ohio and Texas Tech. A class-high 48% of his targets came on deep routes, though he played a more well-rounded role in 2025 -- his lone season with the Red Raiders. Virgil ran a 4.57 40-yard dash at 187 pounds at the combine, which works out to a poor speed score of 86. Virgil will battle Kendrick Bourne for No. 3 duties behind Marvin Harrison Jr. and Michael Wilson. He's off the short-term fantasy radar.

Levis is entering his fourth NFL season. Levis, who missed all of 2025 with a shoulder injury, was the Titans' starter for most of his first two seasons, but simply wasn't up to the task. He totaled 21 pass TDs and 16 INTs in 21 games, while not adding much with his legs (240 yards and one TD). In 2024, he appeared in only 12 games (nine full) and still finished in the top seven in INTs and times sacked. Levis is aggressive (he ranked in the top five in average depth of throw both seasons), but the lack of efficiency and rushing contributions keeps him well off the fantasy radar. He'll barely be worth an add in superflex leagues, even if given the chance to start.

outlooksByWeek.3: Arian Smith has an extremely limited role for the Jets heading into a Week 3 matchup with the Lions. He has been bumped up to No. 4 on the team's depth chart following Omar Cooper being placed on IR, but Smith still logged just one offensive snap in Week 2. With wideouts Garrett Wilson and Adonai Mitchell, capable tight ends, and solid running backs, the Jets offense can't support much more, even in an inviting matchup with a Detroit secondary that's allowed the sixth-most fantasy points to wideouts.

player.seasonOutlook: Burks was selected by the Colts in the seventh round of April's draft. Burks is a small receiver who has experience as both a primary perimeter receiver (under 25% slot in 2023 and 2025) and a primary slot (over 80% slot in 2022 and 2024). He had productive seasons at both Purdue and Oklahoma, though his overall efficiency is fairly poor across the board. That includes an ugly 6.4 YPT and 1.37 YPRR, both of which rank near the basement of this rookie WR class. He showed very well athletically at the combine, including a 4.30 40-yard dash and class-best marks in the vertical (42.5) and bench press (26 reps). Burks is a longshot for 2026 fantasy value.

Law was selected by the Lions in the fifth round of April's draft. Law is a short-area/slot target who played a limited role in three seasons at Alabama (33 catches in 34 games) prior to delivering a 53-540-3 receiving line at Kentucky last season. Law's career 4.2 aDOT is lowest in this WR rookie class, but his 9.1 RAC and 78% catch rate rank first. He'll battle for a returner/depth receiver role and isn't a fantasy option.

Henderson was selected by the Seahawks in the sixth round of April's draft. Henderson is a thin receiver with small hands who has experience playing inside and out (career 38% slot rate). A converted running back, Henderson was limited to five catches in three seasons at Alabama prior to making a leap to a 45-766-5 receiving line (22% target share) in his lone season at Kansas. Henderson was cut in late August and will attempt to work his way back onto an active roster.

Koziol was selected by the Jaguars in the fifth round of April's draft. Across 49 collegiate games at Houston and Ball State, Koziol produced 349 targets, 237 receptions, 2,234 yards, 24 TDs, a 23% target share and a 24% air yard share. All six stats easily top this TE rookie class and that production included a massive 94-839-8 showing in 2024. Koziol has work to do as a blocker, but his size and production suggest there's clear receiving upside. He's worth stashing in dynasty, but doesn't have a path to short-term value behind Brenton Strange and likely fellow rookie Nick Boerkircher.

Carr reportedly considered a return after sitting out the 2025 season, but did not end up signing with a team. He played pretty well during his two-year run with the Saints (including finishing in the top 12 in completion percentage, YPA and QBR in 2024), but injuries cost him seven games in 2024 and he remained an underwhelming fantasy option. Even after a strong start to that 2024 season (21-plus fantasy points in Weeks 1 and 2), Carr ended up contributing 15.1 fantasy PPG in 10 games, which ranked 19th for the season. Incredibly, that matches his best fantasy showing since his career-best 10th in 2016. Carr is a solid passer, but he simply doesn't run enough (below 110 yards in four straight seasons, with one TD during the span) to provide high-end fantasy output.

outlooksByWeek.3: KhaDarel Hodge may be asked to step into a larger role for the 49ers in Week 3 versus Arizona. Hodge has just one catch (on one target) for 18 yards so far this season, but he logged 17 offensive snaps Sunday versus Miami after playing just one snap in Week 1. San Francisco will likely be without No. 3 wideout Demarcus Robinson (ankle) against the Cardinals, and No. 1 WR Mike Evans picked up a hip injury Week 2, leaving the door open for Hodge to get more opportunities. Through two weeks, Arizona ranks in the bottom half of the league in most categories versus wideouts.

player.seasonOutlook: Royer was selected by the Browns in the fifth round of April's draft. After barely seeing the field during three seasons at Ohio State, Royer broke out with a 50-522-3 receiving line (21% target share) in 2024, prior to dipping to 29-416-4 (10%) in 2025. He has solid size with big hands and could emerge as a versatile depth option. Once back on the field, he'll compete for reps behind Harold Fannin Jr. this season.
